nĩwaĩlĩte kũnengwa
translation:
Naye mrembo tausi alicheza densi
kidogo na kisha akajaribu kuliita
jua, "Jua, jua, tafadhali rudi." Lakini
jua lilikataa kujitokeza.
Wanyama wote walijaribu kuliita
jua, mmoja baada ya mwingine.
Lakini jua halikumsikiliza yeyote.
Hatimaye, jogoo alijitokeza kuliita
jua. Kila mmoja alimcheka.
Lakini Simba kama kiongozi mzuri,
alisema, "Tumpe jogoo nafasi naye

text:
Nzamba nĩ wasongie
mbee na kwa ũuu asya,
"Kookoondokoo-koo."
Kĩla mũndũ nĩwaseng'ie
nũndũ sua nĩyaumĩlile
vanini uungu wa kĩĩma.
translation:
The rooster stepped forward and
gently crowed, "Kookoodokoo koo."
To everyone's surprise, the sun
peeped out a little from behind the
hill.

text:
Nzamba nĩ wasongie
mbee na kwa ũuu asya,
"Kookoondokoo-koo."
Kĩla mũndũ nĩwaseng'ie
nũndũ sua nĩyaumĩlile
vanini uungu wa kĩĩma.
translation:
Jogoo alisimama mbele
ya wanyama wote, na
taratibu akawika,
"kookoodookoo-koo."
Jua lilianza kuchomoza
kutoka nyuma ya
mlima.
Wanyama wote
walishangaa kuona
haya.

text:
Nzamba nĩwaisye ĩngĩ kwa
ũkũmbaũ, " KookoondoKOO-KOO..."
Sua nĩyaumĩlangile ĩngĩ ĩũlũ vanini.
Nzamba nĩwaisye ĩla ya katatũ na
waasya mũnene na ũkũmbaũ, "
KOOKOONDOKOO-KOO..." na sua
yambata ĩũlũ na yakenũka.
Nyamũ syonthe sya kĩthekanĩ
nĩsyew'ie mũyo na andũ namo
mew'a mena ũthasyo.
translation:
The rooster crowed again, this time a little boldly,
"KookoodoKOO-KOO..."
The sun came up a little higher. The rooster crowed
for the third time. This time it was louder and bolder,
"KOOKOODOKOO-KOO..." and the sun rose high and
bright.
There was light everywhere.
The animals were delighted and the humans felt
relieved.

text:
Nzamba nĩwaisye ĩngĩ kwa
ũkũmbaũ, " KookoondoKOO-KOO..."
Sua nĩyaumĩlangile ĩngĩ ĩũlũ vanini.
Nzamba nĩwaisye ĩla ya katatũ na
waasya mũnene na ũkũmbaũ, "
KOOKOONDOKOO-KOO..." na sua
yambata ĩũlũ na yakenũka.
Nyamũ syonthe sya kĩthekanĩ
nĩsyew'ie mũyo na andũ namo
mew'a mena ũthasyo.
translation:
Jogoo aliwika tena kwa nguvu zaidi,
"KookooDOO-koo..." Jua lilichomoza
zaidi.
Jogoo akawika kwa mara ya tatu,
"KOOKOODoKOO ..." jua likapanda
juu zaidi na kung'aa.
Kukawa na mwangza kila mahali.
Wanyama wote walifurahia.
Nao binadamu wakaridhika kwa
kuona mwangaza.

text:
Nyamũ sya kĩthekanĩ
nĩsyeiy'e andũ
mekatate ĩngĩ kũwaa
sua na andũ metĩkĩla.
Kuma mũthenya ũsu
nzamba yasya kĩoko
sua nĩyumaa na
ĩkamulĩka matu.
translation:
The animals asked the human
beings not to kill the sun and they
agreed.
Ever since that day, when the
rooster crows in the morning, the
sun rises and shines in the sky.

text:
Nyamũ sya kĩthekanĩ
nĩsyeiy'e andũ
mekatate ĩngĩ kũwaa
sua na andũ metĩkĩla.
Kuma mũthenya ũsu
nzamba yasya kĩoko
sua nĩyumaa na
ĩkamulĩka matu.
translation:
Wanyama waliwaagiza
binadamu wasiliue jua.
Tangu siku hiyo, jogoo
huwika kila asubuhi.
Nalo jua lisikiapo sauti
ya jogoo, huchomoka
na kuangaza duniani.

text:
Tene, tene vyu Ngai wa itu Nyame
avithite ngewa syonthe isandukuni
ya muti matuni. Kuu nthi andu
mayai na ngewa sya utavanya na
mai athatu. Makulya Anansi
mbuavui mbui amatethye.
translation:
Long, long ago, the Sky God,
Nyame, kept all stories locked in a
wooden box, high in the sky.
People down on earth had no
stories to tell and they were very
sad.
They asked Anansi the clever Spider
to help them.

text:
Tene, tene vyu Ngai wa itu Nyame
avithite ngewa syonthe isandukuni
ya muti matuni. Kuu nthi andu
mayai na ngewa sya utavanya na
mai athatu. Makulya Anansi
mbuavui mbui amatethye.
translation:
Hapo zamani za kale, Mungu wa
Mbinguni, Nyamae, alizifungia
hadithi zote kwenye sanduku la
mbao, huko juu.
Watu hapa duniani walihuzunika
sana kwa kuwa hawakuhadithiana.
Wakamwuliza Anansi, buibui,
mwerevu awasaidie.

text:
Anansi aseuvya ulwalui muasa na
atwaia w'o mwii wake waina usasi
nginya ituni.
"No unenge ngewa mwa" akulya
Ngai wa matuni. Na Nyame atheka
Anansi muno na amwia " oo, ngewa
ii ni sya thooa munene, na
ndutonya kusyivia kavwavuli kaa".
translation:
Anansi spun a long thread, and
climbed up his sticky thread all the
way to heaven.
"Can I have the stories, please?" he
asked the Sky God.
But Nyame laughed at Anansi and
said, "Oh, these are very expensive
stories. You wouldn't be able to pay
for them, little spider."

text:
Anansi aseuvya ulwalui muasa na
atwaia w'o mwii wake waina usasi
nginya ituni.
"No unenge ngewa mwa" akulya
Ngai wa matuni. Na Nyame atheka
Anansi muno na amwia " oo, ngewa
ii ni sya thooa munene, na
ndutonya kusyivia kavwavuli kaa".
translation:
Anansi alisokota utando mrefu
unaonata, akautumia kupanda hadi
mbinguni.
"Tafadhali nipe hadithi?" Anansi
alimwambia Mungu wa Mbinguni.
Lakini Nyamae alimcheka Anansi
akisema, "Hadithi hizi ni ghali mno.
Hutaweza kuzilipia, buibui mdogo,
wee."

text:
"Thooa wasyo ni mwau" Anansi
akulya "Mbetee nyamu itatu mbai
na syi mwoo," Nyame asungia "Ngo
yina maeo mavwaa matumo,
Nzweei itong'aa andu na nzoka
imelasya andu onthe.
Atheka na atheka, onaa ngwa syake
to syai vandu vaseo.
translation:
"How much do the stories cost?"
asked Anansi.
"You'll have to bring me three rare
and fierce animals," Nyame
answered, "A leopard with sharp
teeth like spears, a hornet that
stings people, and a snake that
swallows people whole."
He laughed and laughed. He
thought his stories were quite safe.

text:
"Thooa wasyo ni mwau" Anansi
akulya "Mbetee nyamu itatu mbai
na syi mwoo," Nyame asungia "Ngo
yina maeo mavwaa matumo,
Nzweei itong'aa andu na nzoka
imelasya andu onthe.
Atheka na atheka, onaa ngwa syake
to syai vandu vaseo.
translation:
"Hadithi hugharimu pesa ngapi?"
Anansi aliuliza."
"Itabidi uniletee wanyama watatu
wakali na wa kipekee", Nyamae
alijibu, "chui mwenye meno makali
kama mkuki, nyigu anayewauma
watu, na nyoka anayewameza
watu."
Alicheka na kucheka. Alidhani
kwamba hadithi zake zilikuwa
salama.

text:
Anansi atheaa nthi na aitumia ula
ulwalui na avika avindiisya,
avindiisya na akwata usunguio.
Enza iima iluku na akunika na muti
na kiko na enuka aee liu wa wioo.
Kioko vate ngui, Ngo niwalikite
iimani yiu. Akalang'a kila vandu
ateo nde atonya kumaala.
translation:
So Anansi climbed slowly back
down his sticky thread to the earth.
He thought and he thought, and he
came up with a plan.
He dug a deep hole, covered it with
branches and dirt so it was hidden,
and he went home for supper. In the
morning, sure enough, a leopard
had fallen into his pit. He was
furiously scratching at the side of
the pit, but he couldn't get out.

text:
Anansi atheaa nthi na aitumia ula
ulwalui na avika avindiisya,
avindiisya na akwata usunguio.
Enza iima iluku na akunika na muti
na kiko na enuka aee liu wa wioo.
Kioko vate ngui, Ngo niwalikite
iimani yiu. Akalang'a kila vandu
ateo nde atonya kumaala.
translation:
Kwa hivyo Anansi alishuka pole pole
chini. Aliwaza na kuwazua kisha
akapata mpango.
Alichimba shimo refu, akalifunika
kwa matawi na udongo ili
lisionekane, kisha akaenda
nyumbani.
Asubuhi iliyofuata chui alikuwa
ameanguka kwenye shimo. Alikuwa
akikwaruza kuta za shimo kwa
ghadahbu.

text:
"Eka ngutethye munyanyawa"
Anansi aneena, "komeea tumiti tuu
ngukusye ngumalukye". Anansi
alingiliila ulwalui wake wai na usasi
Ngoni vamwe na tumiti na
amikusya amitwaa ituni
kumy'onanyia kula kwai Ngai wa
matu. Ateo nyamu atheka na
amukulya na amukulya " ila ingi ili
syiva.
translation:
"Oh let me help you, my dear
friend!" said Anansi. "Just lie down
on these sticks and I'll pull you out."
Anansi wound his sticky web round
the leopard and the sticks, and
pulled him up to heaven to show
the Sky God.
But Nyame just laughed and said,
"Where are the other two?"

text:
"Eka ngutethye munyanyawa"
Anansi aneena, "komeea tumiti tuu
ngukusye ngumalukye". Anansi
alingiliila ulwalui wake wai na usasi
Ngoni vamwe na tumiti na
amikusya amitwaa ituni
kumy'onanyia kula kwai Ngai wa
matu. Ateo nyamu atheka na
amukulya na amukulya " ila ingi ili
syiva.
translation:
"Hebu nikusaidie, rafiki yangu."
Anansi alisema." "Hebu lalia vijiti
hivi halafu nitakuvuta nje."
Anansi akautungia utando wake
unaonata, kwa mwili wa chui, na
vijiti, kisha akamvuta hadi juu kwa
Mungu wa Mbinguni.
Lakini, Nyamae alimcheka akauliza,
"Wale wengine wawili wako wapi?"

text:
Kwou Anansi atheea ingi kumantha
kyumbe kya keli. Avindiisya na
avindiisya na akwata usungio. Oosa
kikuu kya kiw'u na athi vale Nzweei
syekalaa mutini. Etikiisya kiw'u
kimwe ndalani syoo. Na atema
ithangu ya yiu na ekunikilya mutwe
na eyitikisya kiwu kingi mwiini wake
wonthe.
translation:
So Anansi went back down to earth
to get the second creature. He
thought and he thought and he
came up with a plan.
He took a gourd full of water and
went to the tree where the hornets
lived. He poured out some of the
water all over their nest. Then he
cut a leaf from a banana tree and
held it over his head, and he poured
the rest of the water all over
himself.

text:
Kwou Anansi atheea ingi kumantha
kyumbe kya keli. Avindiisya na
avindiisya na akwata usungio. Oosa
kikuu kya kiw'u na athi vale Nzweei
syekalaa mutini. Etikiisya kiw'u
kimwe ndalani syoo. Na atema
ithangu ya yiu na ekunikilya mutwe
na eyitikisya kiwu kingi mwiini wake
wonthe.
translation:
Kwa hivyo, anansi alirudi tena ardhini kumtafuta
mnyama wa pili. Alifikiri, akafikiri na hatimaye
akaibuka na wazo.
Alichukuwa kibuyu kilichojaa maji na kwenda kwenye
mti walimoishi nyigu. Akamwagilia nyumba ya nyigu
maji mpaka ikalowa kabisa.
Kisha akatafuta jani la mgomba akajikinga nalo
kichwani, halafu akajimwagilia maji yaliyobaki, kila
sehemu ya mwili.

text:
"Inywi nzweei, umaalukai mwone,
nikukua! mituki, likai kikuuni
kyakwa na mwikauiwe" nzweei
siendete kuwiwa kwoou syalika
kikuuni kya Anansi.
translation:
He called out to the hornets, "Hey
hornets! Come see! It is raining!
Quick - get inside my gourd and it
will keep all of you dry."
Hornets don't like to get wet, so
they all flew into Anansi's gourd.

text:
"Inywi nzweei, umaalukai mwone,
nikukua! mituki, likai kikuuni
kyakwa na mwikauiwe" nzweei
siendete kuwiwa kwoou syalika
kikuuni kya Anansi.
translation:
Kisha akawaita manyigu, "Aisee
manyigu! Njooni mwone! Mvua
inanyesha! Haraka – ingieni ndani
ya kibuyu changu ili mjikinge na
mvua.
Manyigu hawapendi kulowa maji;
kwa hivyo, walikimbilia ndani ya
kibuyu cha Anansi.

text:
Anansi aseuvya ulwalui ukunikite
kkuu wethia Nzweei siumaluka
onasyatata. Aikua aitwaia Ngai wa
matuni ituni. Na Nyame asya "ya
mwisyo yiva"? Ateo ndathekaa
muno.
translation:
Then Anansi quickly spun a web
across the opening so the hornets
couldn't get out no matter how
much they buzzed.
He carried them up to heaven and
showed them to the Sky God.
But Nyame just said, "Where's the
last one?" (He wasn't laughing so
much anymore.)

text:
Anansi aseuvya ulwalui ukunikite
kkuu wethia Nzweei siumaluka
onasyatata. Aikua aitwaia Ngai wa
matuni ituni. Na Nyame asya "ya
mwisyo yiva"? Ateo ndathekaa
muno.
translation:
Kwa haraka, Anansi aliutungia
utando wake kwenye mlango ili
manyigu wasitoke kamwe.
Akawabeba wote hadi juu kwa
Mungu wa Mbinguni.
Lakini Nyamae akasema, "Mnyama
wa mwisho yu wapi?" (Wakati huu
hakucheka).

text:
Kwoou Anansi atheea nthi na
avindiisya na avindiisya ateo
ndaamanya undu ukwika.
Niwakulilye muka ula wai na
usungio museo.
Vamwe moona uvonge muasa
muthungu waina tuvonge tunini
twai na vinya. Ila mavikie usini vala
Nzoka yatuaa mambiisya ngananio.
"Uvonge uu ni muasa" "aiyee ti
muasa", "ii ni w'o".
translation:
So Anansi went down to earth
again. He thought and thought and
he thought, but he couldn't come
up with a plan. So he asked his wife,
who had a very good idea.
Together they found a good long
thick branch and some strong vines.
When they got near the stream
where the snake lived, they began
to argue.
"The branch is longer!"
"No, it isn't!"
"Yes it is!"

text:
Kwoou Anansi atheea nthi na
avindiisya na avindiisya ateo
ndaamanya undu ukwika.
Niwakulilye muka ula wai na
usungio museo.
Vamwe moona uvonge muasa
muthungu waina tuvonge tunini
twai na vinya. Ila mavikie usini vala
Nzoka yatuaa mambiisya ngananio.
"Uvonge uu ni muasa" "aiyee ti
muasa", "ii ni w'o".
translation:
Kwa hivyo, Anansi akarudi ardhini tena. Alifikiri na
kufikiri, lakini hakuna wazo zuri lililomjia akilini.
Basi akamwuliza mkewe aliyekuwa na wazo bora
sana.
Walishirikiana kutafuta kijiti kimoja kirefu na kamba
dhabiti.
Walipofika karibu na mto alimoishi nyoka, walianza
kubishana. "Kijiti hiki ni kirefu zaidi!" "hapana si
kirefu!" "Ndio, ni kirefu!"

text:
O mituki Nzoka yaumaluuka na
yamakulya meneenanisya kyau? "Ni
nenanasya na kiveti kyakwa"
Anansi asya. "Kyasya muti uu ni
muasa kuukila ateo nyie
ndiwitikila." "Kwawo ni muasa
kuvituka muti uu" Nzoka yasya. " Ni
muasa muno, ni Nzoka nene"
nthimei na muti wenyu.
translation:
Soon the snake came out and asked
what the argument was.
"I was arguing with my wife," said
Anansi. "She says this stick is
longer than you are. But I don't
agree."
"Of course I'm longer than that
stick!" said the snake.
"I'm very long! I'm a huge snake!
Just put your stick next to me and
measure!"

text:
O mituki Nzoka yaumaluuka na
yamakulya meneenanisya kyau? "Ni
nenanasya na kiveti kyakwa"
Anansi asya. "Kyasya muti uu ni
muasa kuukila ateo nyie
ndiwitikila." "Kwawo ni muasa
kuvituka muti uu" Nzoka yasya. " Ni
muasa muno, ni Nzoka nene"
nthimei na muti wenyu.
translation:
Mara nyoka akatokea kwenye maji akawauliza
sababu ya mabishano yao.
"Mke wangu anasema kwamba kijiti hiki ni kirefu
kuliko wewe," Anansi alisema. "Lakini mimi
sikubaliani naye."
"Lakini ni wazi kwamba mimi ni mrefu kuliko kijiti
hicho!" nyoka alisema. "Mimi ni nyoka mrefu sana!
Hebu weka kijiti karibu nami nijipime."

text:
Kwou Anansi eeka uu na
amyoveanisya na muti na tuuvonge
nikana ilunngale. Amy'ova vyu,
Anansi amitwaa ituni.
translation:
So Anansi did that, and he tied the
snake to the stick with his vine to
keep him straight.
When he was all tied up, Anansi
took the snake up to heaven.

text:
Kwou Anansi eeka uu na
amyoveanisya na muti na tuuvonge
nikana ilunngale. Amy'ova vyu,
Anansi amitwaa ituni.
translation:
Anansi alifanya hivyo.
Kisha akamfunga yule nyoka
kwenye kijiti kile kwa kutumia
kamba ili kumnyoosha sawasawa.
Baada ya kumfunga huyo nyoka
vizuri, alimbeba hadi juu mbinguni.

text:
Nyame ai no muvaka etikile kana
Anansi niwaiva ituvi. Avingua
isanduku ya muti na anenge ngewa
syonthe Anansi. Anansi aete ngewa
syoonthe ena usindi nthi. Atavya
muka na nyamu ingi vamwe na
andu. Nundu ngewa nisyakuewa ti
sya kuia masandukuni ma muti.
translation:
Nyame had to admit that Anansi
had paid his price. So he went to his
wooden box, opened the lid, and
gave all the stories to Anansi.
Anansi carried the stories
triumphantly down to earth.
He shared them with his wife, and
with all the other animals and
people.
Stories are for telling, not for
keeping in wooden boxes.

text:
Nyame ai no muvaka etikile kana
Anansi niwaiva ituvi. Avingua
isanduku ya muti na anenge ngewa
syonthe Anansi. Anansi aete ngewa
syoonthe ena usindi nthi. Atavya
muka na nyamu ingi vamwe na
andu. Nundu ngewa nisyakuewa ti
sya kuia masandukuni ma muti.
translation:
Nyamae akaridhika kwamba Anansi alikuwa ametoa
malipo ya kutosha.
Basi akafungua sanduku lake la mbao, na akampa
Anansi hadithi.
Anansi alizibeba hadithi hizo kwa ushindi mkubwa
hadi ardhini.
Akazigawa kwa mke wake, na watu wengine pamoja
na wanyama, kwa sababu hadithi ni za kuhadithia
wala si za kuficha kwenye sanduku.

text:
Mama ni ukususya ndoo
ndune.
translation:
Mama is filling a red
bucket.

text:
Abongile ni ukuthauka
na iloli itune.
translation:
Abongile is playing with
a red truck.

text:
Deon ni ukwete malaa
matune.
translation:
Deon is holding red
flowers.

text:
Mwendwau niwikite
vulana ndune.
translation:
Aunty is wearing a red
jersey.

text:
Ve isua itune iulu wa
umau.
translation:
There is a red sun
above Grandpa.

text: Ve kivi kivi ndune leluni.
translation:
There is a red scooter
parked in the street.

text:
Ing'ala itune yi mauni
ma Babalwa.
translation:
A red lizard is on
Babalwa's lap.

text:
Ngali ya uvosya mwaki
ndune yi Kiseseni.
translation:
A red fire engine is at
the fire station.

text:
Uu ni Sibahle ekiite
vulana ndune.
translation:
Here is Sibahle wearing
a red top.

text:
Etata kwikia makovo
matune.
translation:
She is trying on red
boots.

text: Mai kuaniiya!
translation: They don't fit!

text:
Tene tene vyũ, kũyaĩ kĩvindu ndũanĩ
ya Opio. Andũ makomaa manoa na
methũkũma masalũkĩtye.
translation:
Long ago, there was no night in
Opio's village.
People slept when they were tired
and worked when they were awake.

text:
Tene tene vyũ, kũyaĩ kĩvindu ndũanĩ
ya Opio. Andũ makomaa manoa na
methũkũma masalũkĩtye.
translation:
Hapo zamani za kale hapakuwa na
usiku katika kijiji cha kina Opio.
Watu walilala wakati wowote ule
waliposikia uchovu. Walifanya kazi
walipokuwa hawajalala.

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe Opio aĩna ũtanu
mwingĩ nũndũ nĩw'o waĩ mũthenya
wake wa mbee kũthi kũsyĩma
eweka. Opio nĩwosie makitĩ na
aumala ndũanĩ. Kavinda kanini
kathela makitĩ nĩmanzĩe
kũsembany'a nzaaĩ.
Opio nĩwamatĩĩe na asemba kĩlungu
kya masaa maingĩ. Anoa
nĩwathũmũaa na ĩndĩ esemba ĩngĩ.
Ndaona makitĩ make.
translation:
One day Opio went out hunting with
his dogs. After a short time, his
dogs started to chase an antelope.
Opio followed them. He ran for
many hours.
Every time he became tired, he
rested. Then he would run again.
But he could not find his dogs.

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe Opio aĩna ũtanu
mwingĩ nũndũ nĩw'o waĩ mũthenya
wake wa mbee kũthi kũsyĩma
eweka. Opio nĩwosie makitĩ na
aumala ndũanĩ. Kavinda kanini
kathela makitĩ nĩmanzĩe
kũsembany'a nzaaĩ.
Opio nĩwamatĩĩe na asemba kĩlungu
kya masaa maingĩ. Anoa
nĩwathũmũaa na ĩndĩ esemba ĩngĩ.
Ndaona makitĩ make.
translation:
Siku moja Opio alienda kuwinda na
mbwa wake. Baada ya muda mfupi,
mbwa waliona paa wakaanza
kumfukuza. Opio aliwafuata.
Alikimbia kwa masaa mengi. Kila
alipochoka alipumzika na kisha
kuanza kukimbia tena. Lakini
hakuwaona mbwa wake.

text:
Ĩtina wa matukũ maingĩ nĩwavikie
ndũanĩ yaĩna andũ anini mailye
mbee wa nyũmba syoo. Nĩwendie
nyũmbanĩ ĩmwe na eea mwene,
"nĩsembanĩtye na Nzaaĩ ĩvinda ĩasa
mũno na nenda kũthũmũa."Mwene
nyũmba nĩwaisye, "ĩkala nthĩ
ũthũmũe. Nũkwenda ũkĩ?" Opio
nĩwew'aa waũni mũno kwou
nĩwanyuie ũkĩ na akoma.
translation:
After many days, he came to a
village. He went to one of the
houses and said to the owner, "I
have chased an antelope for a long
time and I am very tired. I want to
rest."
The man said, "Sit down and rest.
Would you like some beer?"
Opio was very thirsty so he drank
some. Then he went to sleep.

text:
Ĩtina wa matukũ maingĩ nĩwavikie
ndũanĩ yaĩna andũ anini mailye
mbee wa nyũmba syoo. Nĩwendie
nyũmbanĩ ĩmwe na eea mwene,
"nĩsembanĩtye na Nzaaĩ ĩvinda ĩasa
mũno na nenda kũthũmũa."Mwene
nyũmba nĩwaisye, "ĩkala nthĩ
ũthũmũe. Nũkwenda ũkĩ?" Opio
nĩwew'aa waũni mũno kwou
nĩwanyuie ũkĩ na akoma.
translation:
Baada ya siku nyingi alijipata katika
kijiji kingine. Akaingia kwa nyumba
moja akamwambia mwenye
nyumba, "Nimekuwa nikimfukuza
paa kwa muda mrefu na sasa
nimechoka. Nahitaji kupumzika."
Mwenye nyumba akamwambia,
"Ebu keti upumzike. Je, ungependa
pombe kidogo?" Kwa vile Opio
alikuwa na kiu alikunywa pombe
kidogo kisha akalala.

text:
Akũkĩla ndonaa nthĩ. Nĩwavingũie na
kũvĩnga metho make mavinda
maingĩ na anzĩĩa kwona ũla mũndũ
ailye mbee wa nyũmba. Nĩweie
mũndũ ũsu, "ũnengie kĩndũ kĩthũku
mũno; ndĩkwona nesa."
translation:
When he woke up, he couldn't see.
He opened and closed his eyes
many times.
"You have given me something very
bad to drink," he said to the man. "I
can't see properly anymore!"
"There is nothing wrong with you,"
the man replied. "It's night now.
Haven't you ever seen night? When
the day leaves, the night comes."

text:
Akũkĩla ndonaa nthĩ. Nĩwavingũie na
kũvĩnga metho make mavinda
maingĩ na anzĩĩa kwona ũla mũndũ
ailye mbee wa nyũmba. Nĩweie
mũndũ ũsu, "ũnengie kĩndũ kĩthũku
mũno; ndĩkwona nesa."
translation:
Alipoamka alishindwa kuona.
Alifunga na kufungua macho yake
mara nyingi. "Ulinipa kinywaji
kibaya," alimwambia mwenye
nyumba. "Siwezi tena kuona
sawasawa."

text:
Mwene nyũmba nĩwamũie, "vaĩ
kĩndũ kĩthũku naku. Oyu nĩ ũtukũ.
Nũndũ ũtoona ũtukũ. Mũthenya
wathi, ũtukũ nĩũkaa. Twĩthĩwaa na
masaa ĩkũmi na elĩ ma ũtukũ.
Tũthũmũa ũtukũ na twĩthũkũma
mũthenya. Wĩkalaa va? Ndũanĩ
yenyu ndĩ ũtukũ ĩĩ?"
Opio nĩwakũlilye makũlyo maingĩ
ĩũlũ wa ũtukũ nũndũ nĩwendie ũtukũ
mũno. Ndaakoma ĩngĩ; manenie na
mwene nyũmba mbaka kwakya.
Opio nĩwendie kwĩkala mũthenya
ũngĩ nĩkana one ũtukũ ũkũka ĩngĩ.
translation:
Opio asked many questions about
the night. He began to like it very
much.
He and his new friend talked until
morning.
He stayed for another day so that
he could see the night come again.

text:
Mwene nyũmba nĩwamũie, "vaĩ
kĩndũ kĩthũku naku. Oyu nĩ ũtukũ.
Nũndũ ũtoona ũtukũ. Mũthenya
wathi, ũtukũ nĩũkaa. Twĩthĩwaa na
masaa ĩkũmi na elĩ ma ũtukũ.
Tũthũmũa ũtukũ na twĩthũkũma
mũthenya. Wĩkalaa va? Ndũanĩ
yenyu ndĩ ũtukũ ĩĩ?"
Opio nĩwakũlilye makũlyo maingĩ
ĩũlũ wa ũtukũ nũndũ nĩwendie ũtukũ
mũno. Ndaakoma ĩngĩ; manenie na
mwene nyũmba mbaka kwakya.
Opio nĩwendie kwĩkala mũthenya
ũngĩ nĩkana one ũtukũ ũkũka ĩngĩ.
translation:
"Hakuna kitu kibaya na macho yako
yako sawasawa," Mwenye nyumba
alimwambia. "Ni usiku sasa hivi.
Kwani hujawahi kuona usiku tena?
Siku ikiisha, usiku hufuata."
Opio aliuliza maswali mengi kuhusu
usiku. Akapendezwa sana na jambo
la usiku.Yeye na rafiki yake mpya
walizungumza hadi asubuhi. Alikaa
kwake kwa siku nyingine moja ili
aone usiku ukiingia tena.

text:
Nĩwakomie mũthenya na okĩla
ũtukũ ũtanavika. Nĩwakũlilye
mwene nyũmba amũtavye ũndũ
ũtonya kwĩka nĩkana atwae ũtukũ
ndũanĩ yake andũ make matonye
kũwona. Opio nĩweiwe athi okone
sivũ.
translation:
The next morning he asked his
friend,
"How can I take the night to my
own village? I want my people to
see the night."
"When it starts to get dark this
evening, walk to your village. If you
look straight in front, the night will
follow you. But you must not look
back. If you look back, the night will
go away."

text:
Nĩwakomie mũthenya na okĩla
ũtukũ ũtanavika. Nĩwakũlilye
mwene nyũmba amũtavye ũndũ
ũtonya kwĩka nĩkana atwae ũtukũ
ndũanĩ yake andũ make matonye
kũwona. Opio nĩweiwe athi okone
sivũ.
translation:
Asubuhi iliyofuata, yule jamaa,
alimweleza Opio, "Giza likianza
kuingia leo tembea kwenda kijijini
kwenu. Ukitembea huku ukiangalia
mbele usiku utakufuata. Hupaswi
kamwe kuangalia nyuma.
Ukiangalia nyuma usiku utapotea."

text:
Sivũ nĩweie Opio atembee athi
ndũanĩ yake wioo ũla waatĩe.
Ndaĩlĩte kũsisya ĩtina nĩkana ũtukũ
ndũkasyoke. Opio nĩwekie ũndũ
wataviwe na anzĩĩa kũtembea
aendete ndũanĩ yake. Nĩwendaa
kũsisya ĩtina ĩndĩ ndatata kwĩka ou.
Nĩwendie mbaka anzĩĩa kwona ndũa
na anyanyae make.
translation:
Opio did as he was told. That
evening, he began to walk towards
his village.
He felt the dark night behind him as
he walked.
He wanted to look back.
But he did not.

text:
Sivũ nĩweie Opio atembee athi
ndũanĩ yake wioo ũla waatĩe.
Ndaĩlĩte kũsisya ĩtina nĩkana ũtukũ
ndũkasyoke. Opio nĩwekie ũndũ
wataviwe na anzĩĩa kũtembea
aendete ndũanĩ yake. Nĩwendaa
kũsisya ĩtina ĩndĩ ndatata kwĩka ou.
Nĩwendie mbaka anzĩĩa kwona ndũa
na anyanyae make.
translation:
Opio alifanya alivyoambiwa. Usiku
huo alianza kutembea akielekea
kijijini kwao.
Alisikia giza la usiku likimfuata
nyuma yake. Alitaka kuangalia
nyuma lakini hakuangalia.

text:
Mona Opio andũ ma ndũa nĩmakĩie.
Nĩmanzĩĩe kũlonza makwasya, "ni
kyaũ watwetee, Opio? Kĩndũ kĩĩ
kĩkwatĩĩe nĩkyũtũaa. Kĩĩ nĩ kĩvindu
kya kyaũ kĩkwatĩe?"
Opio nĩwaisye, "anyanyawa, kĩvindu
kĩĩ nĩ ũtukũ. Mwĩna vw'ĩa; onakwa
naĩna vw'ĩa."
translation:
When he came to his village, the
villagers were afraid.
"What disease have you brought to
us, Opio?" they asked. "What is this
dark thing following you?"
Opio said, "My friends, this dark
thing is called night. Now you are
afraid and I was afraid, too."

text:
Mona Opio andũ ma ndũa nĩmakĩie.
Nĩmanzĩĩe kũlonza makwasya, "ni
kyaũ watwetee, Opio? Kĩndũ kĩĩ
kĩkwatĩĩe nĩkyũtũaa. Kĩĩ nĩ kĩvindu
kya kyaũ kĩkwatĩe?"
Opio nĩwaisye, "anyanyawa, kĩvindu
kĩĩ nĩ ũtukũ. Mwĩna vw'ĩa; onakwa
naĩna vw'ĩa."
translation:
Alipofika kijijini kwao, wanakijiji
waliogopa. "Opio, ni ugonjwa gani
huu uliotuletea?" walimwuliza. "Ni
nini hiki cheusi kinachokufuata
nyuma yako?" Opio akawaeleza,
"Ndugu zangu kitu cheusi
kinachonifuata kinaitwa usiku.
Mnavyoogopa ndivyo nilivyoogopa
pia."

text:
"Kyeni kyooka notũthũkũme naw'o
ũtukũ wooka tũkũthũmũa."
translation:
"But you will learn to like the night.
When the light comes we can work
and when night comes, we can
rest."

text:
"Kyeni kyooka notũthũkũme naw'o
ũtukũ wooka tũkũthũmũa."
translation:
"Lakini hata nyinyi mtapenda usiku.
Mwangaza ukija tutaweza kufanya
kazi. Na usiku ukiingia
tutapumzika."

text: Na ou nĩw'o ũtukũ wokie ndũanĩ ya Opio.
translation: And that is how night came to Opio's village.

text: Na ou nĩw'o ũtukũ wokie ndũanĩ ya Opio.
translation: Na hivyo ndivyo usiku ulivyoingia kijijini kwa kina Opio.

text: Utathi wina langi mwonza.
translation: One day, Hare was out looking for food. He met Elephant, who had a pot of honey. Hare asked Elephant, "Please be kind and carry me. I am weak."

text: Utathi wina langi mwonza.
translation: Siku moja Sungura alienda kutafuta chakula. Njiani, alikutana na Ndovu aliyebeba asali mgongoni. Sungura alimwambia Ndovu, "Tafadhali nibebe. Mimi ni mnyonge."

text: Langi wa mbee yiitawa mutune.
translation: Elephant agreed to carry Hare. Hare got onto Elephant's back and held on tightly. He started eating Elephant's honey straight away!

text: Langi wa mbee yiitawa mutune.
translation: Ndovu alikubali Sungura akadakia mgongo wake. Mara moja, Sungura alianza kula asali ya Ndovu!

text: Kweyu ekiite sati mutune.
translation: Honey began dripping on Elephant's back. When Elephant asked what it was, Hare said that it was from his wound.

text: Kweyu ekiite sati mutune.
translation: Asali ilidondoka kwenye mgongo wa Ndovu. Ndovu alipouliza, Sungura alisema ni maji kutoka kwenye kidonda chake.

text: Langi wa keli ni wa isungwa.
translation: They reached a river and found a large buffalo drinking water.

text: Langi wa keli ni wa isungwa.
translation: Waliufikia mto na kumkuta kiboko mkubwa akinywa maji.

text: Thii ni isungwa.
translation: Hare wanted to know who was stronger, Buffalo or Elephant.

text: Thii ni isungwa.
translation: Sungura alitaka kujua kati ya Ndovu na Kiboko, ni nani aliyekuwa na nguvu kumshinda mwingine.

text: Langi wa wakatatu ni yelo.
translation: They began arguing. Elephant said she was stronger and Buffalo said she was stronger.

text: Langi wa wakatatu ni yelo.
translation: Walianza kubishana. Ndovu alisema yeye ndiye mwenye nguvu zaidi naye Kiboko akasema ni yeye.

text: Itumbi ya kienyeji yina langi wa yelo.
translation: Hare said he had an idea how to find out who was stronger. He asked them to wait for him there.

text: Itumbi ya kienyeji yina langi wa yelo.
translation: Sungura alisema kuwa alijua jinsi ya kutambua aliyekuwa na nguvu zaidi. Aliwaambia wamsubiri.

text: Langi wa kana ni wa ngilini.
translation: Hare came back with a long rope. He tied the one end around Elephant's waist and led her away from the river.

text: Langi wa kana ni wa ngilini.
translation: Sungura alirejea na kamba ndefu. Alimfunga Ndovu kiunoni na kumwelekeza mbali na mto.

text: Iua ni sya ngilini.
translation: Hare tied the other end of the rope around Buffalo's waist and left her near the river.

text: Iua ni sya ngilini.
translation: Sungura alimfunga Kiboko kiunoni na kumuacha pale karibu na mto.

text: Langi wa katano ni mbuluu.
translation: Hare ran and hid himself in a tree. He shouted, "Ready! One, two, three! Pull!"

text: Langi wa katano ni mbuluu.
translation: Sungura alijificha mtini akasema, "Tayari! Moja, mbili, tatu! Vuta sasa!"

text: Matu ni ma mbuluu.
translation: Buffalo and Elephant pulled. Elephant pulled Buffalo.

text: Matu ni ma mbuluu.
translation: Kiboko na Ndovu walivutana. Ndovu alimvuta Kiboko naye Kiboko alimvuta Ndovu.

text: Langi wa thanthatu ni wa mbuluu ngwatu.
translation: Buffalo pulled Elephant. Neither could win.

text: Langi wa thanthatu ni wa mbuluu ngwatu.
translation: Kiboko na Ndovu walivutana lakini, hakuna aliyeshinda.

text: Matunda aa ni ma langi wa mbuluu ngwatu.
translation: From where he was hiding, Hare continued to eat Elephant's honey.

text: Matunda aa ni ma langi wa mbuluu ngwatu.
translation: Sungura aliendelea kula asali ya Ndovu kule mtini.

text: Langi wa mwonza ni wa nthambalau.
translation: After he had finished the honey, he cut the rope closer to Buffalo.

text: Langi wa mwonza ni wa nthambalau.
translation: Baada ya kumaliza kula asali, aliikatia kamba karibu sana na Kiboko.

text:
Ngua yakwa ni ya langi wa nthambalau.
Ni langi niwendete muno!
translation: Elephant fell over hard and hit a tree.

text:
Ngua yakwa ni ya langi wa nthambalau.
Ni langi niwendete muno!
translation: Ndovu aliangukia mti kwa kishindo.

text: Niwise langi syonthe sya utathi?
translation: Hare went to Buffalo and praised her, saying that she was stronger.

text: Niwise langi syonthe sya utathi?
translation: Sungura alimshangilia Kiboko akisema kwamba yeye ndiye mwenye nguvu zaidi.

text: Nonisome.
translation:
Nomsa overhears Jabu and Zodwa talking and she's curious. She asks them what's wrong with cutting the loaf into five pieces for kotas.
Zodwa and Jabu reply together, "A kota is a quarter of a loaf!"
Nomsa still looks confused, so Zodwa explains, "The loaf must be cut into four equal pieces. Otherwise, they are not quarters."

text:
Tene tene vyu vaĩ na
mũndũũme wekalaa na mũka
na kũmwenda mũno.
Mũthenya ũmwe nĩwaendie
kĩthekanĩ. Enzĩanĩ nĩwakomanie
na mwĩĩtu mũasa, mũtheke na
mwanake.
Nĩwamwendie kwa mĩtukĩ.
Mwĩĩtu nake nĩwamwĩtĩkĩlile
omĩtũkĩ ĩndĩ amũtavya kana
enondo ĩmwe tu.
translation:
A long time ago, there was a
man who lived with his wife
whom he loved very much.
One day he took a walk to the
forest. Along the way, he met a
tall, slender, and very beautiful
girl.
He fell in love with her at first
sight. The girl too readily
accepted him.
But she told him that she had
only one breast.

text:
Tene tene vyu vaĩ na
mũndũũme wekalaa na mũka
na kũmwenda mũno.
Mũthenya ũmwe nĩwaendie
kĩthekanĩ. Enzĩanĩ nĩwakomanie
na mwĩĩtu mũasa, mũtheke na
mwanake.
Nĩwamwendie kwa mĩtukĩ.
Mwĩĩtu nake nĩwamwĩtĩkĩlile
omĩtũkĩ ĩndĩ amũtavya kana
enondo ĩmwe tu.
translation:
Hapo kale palikuwa na mtu aliyeishi na mkewe
aliyempenda sana.
Siku moja alikwenda msituni kwa matembezi.
Njiani alikutana na msichana mmoja
mwembamba na mrembo mno.
Alimpenda papo hapo. Msichana vile vile
alimkubali mara moja.
Lakini, msichana alimwambia kuwa alikuwa na
titi moja tu.

text:
Nĩwamũie athi mũsyĩ akatile
mũka nondo ĩmwe amwetee
avikye nondo ilĩ nikana matonye
kũtwaana.
Mũndũũme ũsu nĩwasembie
mũsyĩ, osa kavyũ, avalũkya
mũka nthĩ, na omĩtũkĩ amũtila
nondo.
translation:
So she told him to go home, cut
off one of his wife's breasts and
bring it to her. Then she would
have two breasts, and they
could marry.
The man ran very fast back
home, picked a knife, pounced
on his dear wife, and the breast
was off instantly.

text:
Nĩwamũie athi mũsyĩ akatile
mũka nondo ĩmwe amwetee
avikye nondo ilĩ nikana matonye
kũtwaana.
Mũndũũme ũsu nĩwasembie
mũsyĩ, osa kavyũ, avalũkya
mũka nthĩ, na omĩtũkĩ amũtila
nondo.
translation:
Kwa hivyo alimwambia aende nyumbani, akate
titi moja la mkwewe amletee.
Kwa njia hii angekuwa na matiti mawili hivyo
wangeoana.
Mwanamme alikimbia kwa kasi, akachukuwa
kisu, akamrukia mkewe mpendwa na kukata
titi lake mara moja.

text:
Nĩwasembie asyoka kĩthekanĩ
vala watiĩte mwendwa wake.
Ĩndĩ ndamwĩthĩa. Nĩwamwĩtie
kwa ĩsyitwa na wasya mũnene,
ĩndĩ nĩkwethĩiwe kĩvindyo
kĩnene.
Na ĩndĩ niwew'ie wasya
ũkyasya, "wĩtana nĩkĩ? Nũndũ
ũtesĩ wĩkĩthekanĩ kya
Mũsambwa wa Limbeeletwela?"
translation:
He hurried back to the forest to
where he had left his newfound
darling.
But she was nowhere to be
seen. He called her name very
loudly, but there was complete
silence.
Then he heard a voice saying,
"Why are you calling? Don't you
know that you are in the forest
area of Musambwa kwa
Libeeletwela?"

text:
Nĩwasembie asyoka kĩthekanĩ
vala watiĩte mwendwa wake.
Ĩndĩ ndamwĩthĩa. Nĩwamwĩtie
kwa ĩsyitwa na wasya mũnene,
ĩndĩ nĩkwethĩiwe kĩvindyo
kĩnene.
Na ĩndĩ niwew'ie wasya
ũkyasya, "wĩtana nĩkĩ? Nũndũ
ũtesĩ wĩkĩthekanĩ kya
Mũsambwa wa Limbeeletwela?"
translation:
Aliharakisha kwenda msituni alikomwacha
mpenzi wake mpya.
Lakini hakuwapo. Aliliita jina lake kwa sauti,
lakini ilikuwa kimya tu.
Kisha alisikia sauti ikisema, "Kwa nini unaita?
Kwani hujui kwamba uko katika msitu wa
Musambwa kwa Libeeletwela?"

text:
Ĩla mũndũũme ũsu wew'ie ũu,
nĩwasembie mũsyĩ mĩtũkĩ ta
kĩsasi...
Ĩndĩ nĩwethĩie mũka akw'a.
Nĩwakwatiwe ni kyeva kingĩ na
nũndũ wa ũndũ ũla wekĩte nake
akw'a.
translation:
When the man heard that, he
ran home as fast as a bullet ...
Only to find his wife had just
died.
He was so grief stricken
because of what he had done
that he too died.

text:
Ĩla mũndũũme ũsu wew'ie ũu,
nĩwasembie mũsyĩ mĩtũkĩ ta
kĩsasi...
Ĩndĩ nĩwethĩie mũka akw'a.
Nĩwakwatiwe ni kyeva kingĩ na
nũndũ wa ũndũ ũla wekĩte nake
akw'a.
translation:
Mtu yule aliposikia hivyo,
alikimbia nyumbani kwa kasi
kama risasi...
Alimpata mkewe tayari akiwa
amefariki.
Alihuzunika sana kwa ajili ya
yale alikuwa amefanya. Naye
alitaka kufa.

text:
Tene tene vyũ kwaĩ mũndũ ũmwe ngya na mũka wake. Maĩna kana kamwe ka kelĩtu ketawa Nokũngũ.
Nokũngũ aĩ mwanake na mũthingu.
Asyai make nĩmamwendete mũno.
translation:
Once upon a time there was a poor
man and his wife. They had only
one child, a girl. The child's name
was Nonkungu.
Her parents loved Nonkungu very
much.

text:
Tene tene vyũ kwaĩ mũndũ ũmwe ngya na mũka wake. Maĩna kana kamwe ka kelĩtu ketawa Nokũngũ.
Nokũngũ aĩ mwanake na mũthingu.
Asyai make nĩmamwendete mũno.
translation:
Paliishi mtu maskini na mkewe.
Walikuwa na binti yao mrembo
aliyeitwa Nonkungu.

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe asyai make nĩmavangie kũmũtwaa kwa naũme wake mũthui wetawa Mũtonyama.
Inya nĩwamũseũvĩsye kĩsikati kĩseo kĩna malaa na ivungo na wanyũa.
Nĩwamũseũvĩsye ĩsoa ya wanyũa na ĩndĩ amũtũma ndũanĩ ya naũme.
translation:
One day her parents decided to
send her to stay with her rich Uncle
Mtonyama.
Nonkungu's mother made a special
skirt with ribbon, buttons and
beads.
She also made a beautiful bead
necklace for Nonkungu.
Then she sent her off to her uncle's
village.

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe asyai make nĩmavangie kũmũtwaa kwa naũme wake mũthui wetawa Mũtonyama.
Inya nĩwamũseũvĩsye kĩsikati kĩseo kĩna malaa na ivungo na wanyũa.
Nĩwamũseũvĩsye ĩsoa ya wanyũa na ĩndĩ amũtũma ndũanĩ ya naũme.
translation:
Siku moja wazazi walimtuma
Nonkungu akaishi na mjombake
tajiri.
Mamake alimtengenezea
Nonkungu mkufu wa shanga na
rinda alilolirembesha kwa
shanga.

text:
Aendete Nokũngũ nĩwethĩie kalũsĩ na akakĩla akinyangĩte mavia.
Mũingo Nokũngũ nĩwakomanie na kelĩtu kanini kekĩte ilai.
translation:
On the way Nonkungu came to a
stream. She crossed the stream
using the stepping stones.
On the other side she met a young
girl wearing rags.

text:
Aendete Nokũngũ nĩwethĩie kalũsĩ na akakĩla akinyangĩte mavia.
Mũingo Nokũngũ nĩwakomanie na kelĩtu kanini kekĩte ilai.
translation:
Nonkungu alivuka mto na
kukutana na msichana aliyevaa
matambara.

text:
Kelĩtu nĩkamũkũlilye, "Wendete kũ?" "Nendete kũkethya mama Mũtonyama," Nokũngũ nĩwasũngĩie "Onakwa Mũtonyama nĩ mama na nendete kũmũkethya," kelĩtu nĩkaisye.
Kwou nĩmatembeie vamwe.
translation:
"Where are you going?" asked the
young girl.
"I'm going to visit my Uncle
Mtonyama," said Nonkungu.
"Well, Mtonyama is my uncle, too
and I am also on my way to visit
him," said the young girl.
So they walked on together.

text:
Kelĩtu nĩkamũkũlilye, "Wendete kũ?" "Nendete kũkethya mama Mũtonyama," Nokũngũ nĩwasũngĩie "Onakwa Mũtonyama nĩ mama na nendete kũmũkethya," kelĩtu nĩkaisye.
Kwou nĩmatembeie vamwe.
translation:
"Unaenda wapi?" Yule msichana
alimwuliza.
"Ninamtembelea mjombangu
Mtonyama," Nonkungu alisema.
"Ala! Mtonyama ni mjombangu
pia nami namtembelea," yule
msichana akasema.
Wakatembea pamoja.

text: Mendanga vanini kelĩtu nĩkaisye, "kĩsikati kyaku nĩkĩseo mũno na ĩsoa yaku nĩyanake, vatonyeka nenge nele." Nokũngũ nĩwaumisye kĩsikati na ĩsoa yake na anenge kala kelĩtu.
translation:
Before they had gone very far, the
young girl said, "Your skirt is so
beautiful and your beads are so
pretty. Please let me try them on."
So Nonkungu took off her skirt and
beads and gave them to the young
girl.

text: Mendanga vanini kelĩtu nĩkaisye, "kĩsikati kyaku nĩkĩseo mũno na ĩsoa yaku nĩyanake, vatonyeka nenge nele." Nokũngũ nĩwaumisye kĩsikati na ĩsoa yake na anenge kala kelĩtu.
translation:
Yule msichana akasema, "Rinda
lako ni zuri na mkufu wako
unapendeza. Hebu nivae nione
zitakavyonikaa."
Nonkungu alimpa rinda na
mkufu.

text:
Ĩla kelĩtu kau kaumisye ilai syako nakekĩa ngũa sya Nokũngũ, Nokũngũ nĩwonie kelĩtu kena mwĩthe!
Nokũngũ nĩwew'ie w'ĩa nũndũ nĩwamanyie kelĩtu kau nĩyalyũka.
translation:
When the girl took off her rags and
changed into Nonkungu's clothes,
Nonkungu saw that the young girl
had a tail!
Nonkungu was afraid.
She knew now that the young girl
was really an imbulu.

text:
Ĩla kelĩtu kau kaumisye ilai syako nakekĩa ngũa sya Nokũngũ, Nokũngũ nĩwonie kelĩtu kena mwĩthe!
Nokũngũ nĩwew'ie w'ĩa nũndũ nĩwamanyie kelĩtu kau nĩyalyũka.
translation:
Msichana huyo alipovaa nguo
za
Nonkungu, Nonkungu aligundua
kwamba alikuwa na mkia!
Yule msichana alikuwa Imbulu.

text: Nĩmatembeangie vamwe na Nokũngũ asya, "ndũngĩe kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa." Ĩndĩ yalyũka nĩyaisye, "eka nĩkĩange nginya tũvike mũtĩnĩ ũya." Nĩyaolotile mũtĩ wĩ kĩĩmanĩ.
translation:
They walked on together.
"Please give me back my skirt and
my beads," asked Nonkungu.
But the imbulu answered, "Let me
wear them until we get to that
tree."
She pointed to a tree on the hill.

text: Nĩmatembeangie vamwe na Nokũngũ asya, "ndũngĩe kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa." Ĩndĩ yalyũka nĩyaisye, "eka nĩkĩange nginya tũvike mũtĩnĩ ũya." Nĩyaolotile mũtĩ wĩ kĩĩmanĩ.
translation:
Nonkungu alipomwambia
amrudishie rinda na mkufu,
Imbulu alisema, "Wacha
niendelee kuvaa kidogo."

text:
Ĩla mavikĩĩe mũtĩ ũsu, Nokũngũ nĩwaisye, "ndũngĩe kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa."
"Mbekee tu nĩkĩange nginya tũvike kalũsĩnĩ kala katĩe," yalyũka nĩyaisye. Nokũngũ nĩwetĩkĩlile nũndũ nĩwakĩaa.
translation:
When they reached the tree,
Nonkungu said to the imbulu,
"Please give me back my skirt and
beads."
"Just let me wear them until we get
to the next stream," said the
imbulu.
Nonkungu was afraid, so she
agreed.

text:
Ĩla mavikĩĩe mũtĩ ũsu, Nokũngũ nĩwaisye, "ndũngĩe kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa."
"Mbekee tu nĩkĩange nginya tũvike kalũsĩnĩ kala katĩe," yalyũka nĩyaisye. Nokũngũ nĩwetĩkĩlile nũndũ nĩwakĩaa.
translation:
Baadaye, Nonkungu
alimwambia Imbulu tena,
"Tafadhali nirudishie rinda na
mkufu wangu."
Hata hivyo, Imbulu hakumpatia.

text:
Nĩmavikie kala kalũsĩnĩ na Nokũngũ eea yalyũka, "vatonyeka ndũngĩe kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa."
"Mbekee tu nĩkĩange nginya tũvike kanyũmbanĩ kaala vala iveti isu syile nthĩ," yalyũka nĩyaisye.
Kwou nĩmaendie na mbee.
translation:
At last they reached the stream.
Again Nonkungu asked the imbulu,
"Please give me back my skirt and
my beads."
"Just let me wear them until we get
to that hut where the women are
sitting," said the imbulu.
So they walked on.

text:
Nĩmavikie kala kalũsĩnĩ na Nokũngũ eea yalyũka, "vatonyeka ndũngĩe kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa."
"Mbekee tu nĩkĩange nginya tũvike kanyũmbanĩ kaala vala iveti isu syile nthĩ," yalyũka nĩyaisye.
Kwou nĩmaendie na mbee.
translation:
Waliufikia mto lakini Imbulu
bado hakumrudishia Nonkungu
rinda wala mkufu.

text:
Ĩla mavikie kanyũmbanĩ yalyuka nĩyalutile Nokũngũ ĩtina na yeya iveti ila syaile vau, "syisyai kelĩtu kaa kekĩte ilai. Kambatĩe mũthenya mũima na nenda kasyoke."
Nokũngũ nĩwakwatiwe ni nzoni na asemba evitha kyũũnĩ.
translation:
When they reached the hut, the
imbulu pushed Nonkungu back and
called to the women sitting by the
hut.
"Look at this girl wearing rags. She
has been following me all day. I
wish she would go away," said the
imbulu.
Nonkungu was so ashamed and so
frightened that she ran hid in the
kraal.

text:
Ĩla mavikie kanyũmbanĩ yalyuka nĩyalutile Nokũngũ ĩtina na yeya iveti ila syaile vau, "syisyai kelĩtu kaa kekĩte ilai. Kambatĩe mũthenya mũima na nenda kasyoke."
Nokũngũ nĩwakwatiwe ni nzoni na asemba evitha kyũũnĩ.
translation:
Walipofika kwenye boma,
Imbulu aliwaambia wenyeji
kwamba Nonkungu alikuwa
akimfuata siku nzima.
"Nataka aniondokee."
Nonkungu aliaibika akajificha.

text:
Yalyũka nĩyendie nyũmbanĩ ya Mũtonyama na yamwĩa "ninyie mwĩvau Nokũngũ. Asyai makwa mambĩie nũke kwĩkala naku."
Mũtonyama nĩwathokisye mwĩĩtu ũsu na andũ make mekala nesa na ũthingu na ĩla yalyuka. Ĩndĩ Nokũngũ ekalaa kyũũnĩ na kũya lĩu wa ngitĩ.
translation:
Then the imbulu went to Uncle
Mtonyama's hut. She said sweetly,
"I am your niece, Nonkungu. My
parents sent me to stay with you."
Mtonyama welcomed the young
girl. He and his family were very
kind to the imbulu.
But poor Nonkungu had to sleep in
the kraal and share the dog's food.

text:
Yalyũka nĩyendie nyũmbanĩ ya Mũtonyama na yamwĩa "ninyie mwĩvau Nokũngũ. Asyai makwa mambĩie nũke kwĩkala naku."
Mũtonyama nĩwathokisye mwĩĩtu ũsu na andũ make mekala nesa na ũthingu na ĩla yalyuka. Ĩndĩ Nokũngũ ekalaa kyũũnĩ na kũya lĩu wa ngitĩ.
translation:
Imbulu alimwambia Mtonyama,
"Mimi ni mpwa wako,
Nonkungu. Wazazi wamenituma
niishi nawe."
Walimfurahia sana huku
Nonkungu akilala nje.

text:
Kwi mũthenya Nokũngũ endaa mũũndanĩ akwĩvitha mbembanĩ na akw'ina:
"Thĩna atĩ thĩna nyie. Natũmiwe nĩ tata na inya nũke kwĩkala na mama Mũtonyama. Nzĩanĩ nakomanie na yalyũka na yoosa kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa. Thĩna atĩ thĩna nyie."
translation:
During the day Nonkungu went to
the fields, hid in the corn, and sang:
"Oh misery me, misery me.
I was sent by my father and mother
to stay with my Uncle Mtonyama.
On the way I met an imbulu and she
took my skirt and my beads.
Oh misery me, misery me."

text:
Kwi mũthenya Nokũngũ endaa mũũndanĩ akwĩvitha mbembanĩ na akw'ina:
"Thĩna atĩ thĩna nyie. Natũmiwe nĩ tata na inya nũke kwĩkala na mama Mũtonyama. Nzĩanĩ nakomanie na yalyũka na yoosa kĩsikati kyakwa na ĩsoa yakwa. Thĩna atĩ thĩna nyie."
translation:
Nonkungu aliimba:
Matatizo matatizo!
Wazazi walinituma,
Kwa mjomba Mtonyama,
Kakutana na imbulu,
Nguo zangu kachukua,
Matatizo matatizo!

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe mwanainyaa Mũtonyama ũmwe akĩtembea mĩundanĩ nĩwew'ie wathi ũsu mũseo na wa tei.
Ndamanya vala wathi ũsu waumaa ĩndĩ avika mũsyĩ nĩwatavisye Mũtonyama ndeto sya wathi ũsu.
Mũtonyama ew'a ũu nĩwendie mũũndanĩ na.
translation:
One day, one of Mtonyama's
brothers was walking in the fields.
He heard the strange and beautiful
song.
He didn't know who was singing,
but when he got home, he told
Mtonyama the words.
Mtonyama went into the fields. He
heard the song, and looked until he
found Nonkungu.

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe mwanainyaa Mũtonyama ũmwe akĩtembea mĩundanĩ nĩwew'ie wathi ũsu mũseo na wa tei.
Ndamanya vala wathi ũsu waumaa ĩndĩ avika mũsyĩ nĩwatavisye Mũtonyama ndeto sya wathi ũsu.
Mũtonyama ew'a ũu nĩwendie mũũndanĩ na.
translation:
Nduguye Mtonyama alitembea
shambani na kusikia wimbo
mtamu.
Alirudi nyumbani akamweleza
Mtonyama.
Mtonyama alienda kuusikiliza
akamwona Nonkungu.

text:
Nokũngũ nĩwamũtavisye ũndũ kwekĩkie, ũndũ yalyũka yamũvenie ngũa syake nzeo na yatumwa ekĩa ilai.
Mũtonyama nĩwamwosie na athi nake kwake nake na amũvitha nyũmba nzĩnĩ.
Mũtonyama nĩwesĩ ũndũ ũkũkwatya yalyũka.
translation:
Nonkungu told him what had
happened, how the imbulu had
taken her beautiful clothes.
Mtonyama took her back to his
place and hid her in a hut.
Mtonyama knew what he was going
to do to catch the imbulu.

text:
Nokũngũ nĩwamũtavisye ũndũ kwekĩkie, ũndũ yalyũka yamũvenie ngũa syake nzeo na yatumwa ekĩa ilai.
Mũtonyama nĩwamwosie na athi nake kwake nake na amũvitha nyũmba nzĩnĩ.
Mũtonyama nĩwesĩ ũndũ ũkũkwatya yalyũka.
translation:
Nonkungu alimweleza jinsi
alivyodanganywa na Imbulu.
Mtonyama alimpeleka
nyumbani akapanga
kumwadhibu Imbulu.

text:
Mũtonyama nĩwew'ĩte kana mwĩthe wa yalyũka nĩwendete ĩia na ndwamba kũtia ĩia ũtanywĩte ĩmwe.
Kwou nĩwatavisye aũme make masimbe ĩima ĩnene na makwĩyusũsya na ĩia ĩwaatu.
Nĩwetie eĩtu onthe ma ndũa moke masindane kũtwĩla.
translation:
Mtonyama had heard that an
imbulu's tail loves milk and that it
can't go past milk without drinking
some.
So he told his men to dig a deep
ditch and to fill the ditch with sour
milk.
Then he called all the girls of the
village to take part in a jumping
competition.

text:
Mũtonyama nĩwew'ĩte kana mwĩthe wa yalyũka nĩwendete ĩia na ndwamba kũtia ĩia ũtanywĩte ĩmwe.
Kwou nĩwatavisye aũme make masimbe ĩima ĩnene na makwĩyusũsya na ĩia ĩwaatu.
Nĩwetie eĩtu onthe ma ndũa moke masindane kũtwĩla.
translation:
Mtonyama alisikia kwamba
mkia wa Imbulu ulipenda
kunywa maziwa.
Wafanyi kazi wake walichimba
shimo wakalijaza maziwa.
Wasichana wote kijijini
walishindana kuruka.

text:
Mwĩĩtu ũla wekĩĩte ngũa sya Nokũngũ nĩwakwatiwe nĩ kĩthikii.
Ndendaa kũtwĩla ĩũlũ wa ĩla ĩima nũndũ nĩwesĩ mwĩthe wake ũkew'a waũni wa ĩia.
Kwou nĩwalikile nyũmba na oveanĩsya mwĩthe na mwĩĩ wake alũmya ũndũ vatonyeka.
Na ĩndĩ nĩwendie kũlikana na eĩtu ala angĩ.
translation:
The imbulu was worried. She did
not want to jump over the ditch.
She knew that her tail would be
thirsty for the sour milk.
So she went into a hut and tied her
tail to her body as tightly as she
could. Then she took her place with
the other girls.

text:
Mwĩĩtu ũla wekĩĩte ngũa sya Nokũngũ nĩwakwatiwe nĩ kĩthikii.
Ndendaa kũtwĩla ĩũlũ wa ĩla ĩima nũndũ nĩwesĩ mwĩthe wake ũkew'a waũni wa ĩia.
Kwou nĩwalikile nyũmba na oveanĩsya mwĩthe na mwĩĩ wake alũmya ũndũ vatonyeka.
Na ĩndĩ nĩwendie kũlikana na eĩtu ala angĩ.
translation:
Imbulu alikuwa na hofu.
Alijua mkia wake ungetamani
maziwa.
Aliufunga mkia na kuukazia
kwenye mwili wake.

text:
Eĩtu nĩmanzie kũtwĩla ĩũlũ wa ĩima ũmwe ĩtina wa ũngĩ.
Ĩla ĩvinda ya yalyũka yavikie nĩyatatie kũtwĩla ĩla ĩima ĩndĩ mwĩthe wayo nĩwathalĩkile waĩkusya, waĩkusya, waĩkusya, mũvaka ĩla ĩianĩ ĩwatu.
translation:
One girl after another jumped over
the ditch.
At last it was the imbulu's turn.
She tried to jump high over the
ditch, but her tail broke loose.
The imbulu's tail pulled her down,
down, down into the sour milk.

text:
Eĩtu nĩmanzie kũtwĩla ĩũlũ wa ĩima ũmwe ĩtina wa ũngĩ.
Ĩla ĩvinda ya yalyũka yavikie nĩyatatie kũtwĩla ĩla ĩima ĩndĩ mwĩthe wayo nĩwathalĩkile waĩkusya, waĩkusya, waĩkusya, mũvaka ĩla ĩianĩ ĩwatu.
translation:
Ilipokuwa zamu ya Imbulu
kuruka, mkia wake ulifunguka
ukamvuta chini, chini, chini
kwenye shimo la maziwa.

text:
Yalyũka yendee na kwilita ĩianĩ ĩsu ĩwatu aũme nĩmosũisye ĩima na kĩthangathĩ na mathika yalyũka.
Na ũsu nĩw'o waĩ mũthya wa yalyũka.
Ĩndĩ Nokũngũ nĩwekalile nesa na naũme kwa kĩlungu kĩasa.
Ngewa yathelela vau.
translation:
As the imbulu struggled in the sour
milk, the men quickly filled the
ditch with sand and buried her. That
was the end of the imbulu.
Nonkungu stayed happily with her
uncle for a long, long time.
And that is the end of the story.

text:
Yalyũka yendee na kwilita ĩianĩ ĩsu ĩwatu aũme nĩmosũisye ĩima na kĩthangathĩ na mathika yalyũka.
Na ũsu nĩw'o waĩ mũthya wa yalyũka.
Ĩndĩ Nokũngũ nĩwekalile nesa na naũme kwa kĩlungu kĩasa.
Ngewa yathelela vau.
translation:
Imbulu alipokuwa akitapatapa
ndani ya maziwa, wanaume
waliliziba lile shimo na kumzika.
Nonkungu aliishi na mjombake
kwa furaha kwa miaka mingi.
Na huo ndio mwisho wa hadithi.

text:
Kyumwa kithelu nina
kwatie valua mbiingi.
translation:
Last week I received a
lot of letters.

Wakatatu ninakwatie

text: Niki mwana ukuia?
translation: Why is the baby crying?

text: Niki mwana ukuia?
translation: Kwa nini mtoto analia?

text: Nikwathya ena nzaa.
translation: I think she is hungry.

text: Nikwathya ena nzaa.
translation: Nadhani anahisi njaa.

text: Niki kivisi ni kithatu?
translation: Why is the boy sad?

text: Niki kivisi ni kithatu?
translation:
Kwa nini mvulana
amehuzunika?

text:
Nikwatya kina mea ma
ithe.
translation:
I think he is missing his
father.

text:
Nikwatya kina mea ma
ithe.
translation:
Nadhani anamkosa
baba yake.

text: Niki kelitu ni katanu?
translation: Why is the girl happy?

text: Niki kelitu ni katanu?

Kwa nini msichana
amefurahi?

text: Kena ilinda yeu.
translation: She has a new dress.

text: Kena ilinda yeu.
translation:
Kwa sababu ana rinda
jipya.

text:
Niki mutumia mukuu
ukutheka?
translation:
Why is the old man
laughing?

text:
Niki mutumia mukuu
ukutheka?
translation:
Kwa nini mzee
anacheka?

text:
Nusomie kindu kya
uthekya.
translation: He read a good joke.

text:
Nusomie kindu kya
uthekya.
translation:
Kwa sababu amesoma
kichekesho.

text:
Niki mundu muka
ukukenyeesya itheka?
translation: Why is the lady smiling?

text:
Niki mundu muka
ukukenyeesya itheka?
translation:
Kwa nini mama huyu
anatabasamu?

text:
Niki mundu muka
ukukenyeesya itheka?
translation:
Her children are reading
quietly.

text:
Niki mundu muka
ukukenyeesya itheka?
translation:
Watoto wake wanasoma
kimya kimya.

text: Mundu muka ew'a ata?
translation:
What is this lady
feeling?

text: Mundu muka ew'a ata?
translation:
Mama huyu anahisi
nini?

text: Nikwatya ewa nzoni.
translation:
I think she is feeling
shy.

text: Nikwatya ewa nzoni.
translation: Nadhani anaona haya.

text: Ũũ ni Ngi.
translation: This is Mr Fly.

text: Ũũ nĩ mũtwe mũnene.
translation: This is Mr Big Head.

text:
Ngi and Mũtwe mũnene
maĩ ndũũ. Mũthenya
ũmwe nĩmaendie
kũtembea.
translation:
Mr Big Head and Mr Fly
were friends.
One day, they went for
a walk together.

text:
Nĩmavikie ngũkanĩ ya
ũsĩ na manzĩĩa
kũkananĩsy.
translation:
They came to the edge
of a river, and started
arguing with each
other.
Mr Fly said, "You can't
jump over this river!"
"Yes, I can! It's you who
can't!" replied Mr Big
Head.

text:
"Ndwamba kũkĩla ũsĩ
ũũ!"
"Nonĩkĩle. Niwe
ũtakĩla!"
translation:
"You jump!" said Mr Fly.
"No, you jump first,"
said Mr Big Head.
So Mr Fly flew across
the river.

text:
Ngi nĩwaisye, "we
twĩla!"
"Aiee, we twĩla mbee,"
Mũtwe mũnene
nĩwaisye.
Kwou Ngi nĩwolũkile
akĩla ũsĩ ũsu.
translation:
Then Mr Big Head
jumped into the river.
But his head was so big
that he started to sink.

text:
Mũtwe mũnene
nĩwatwĩlie ũsĩnĩ. Ĩndĩ
nũndũ mũtwe wake waĩ
mũnene ndaalela;
nĩwanzĩĩe kw'indanw'a
nĩ kĩw'ũ.
translation:
Mr Fly laughed, "Hee
hee!"
But he laughed so
much that his mouth
tore in two from one
side to the other!

text:
Sũsũ aĩ vakuvĩ mĩaka mĩongo
mwonza. Aĩ mũthangaau. Mũũndanĩ
kwake avandaa mũvya, mwee,
manga na maiũ. Sũsũ akethaa maiũ
kĩla ĩvinda ya mwaka.
Grandma's garden was wonderful full of sorghum, millet, and cassava.
But best of all were the bananas.
Although Grandma had many
grandchildren, I secretly knew that I
was her favourite. She invited me
often to her house. She also told me
little secrets. But there was one
secret she did not share with me:
where she ripened bananas.
translation:
Grandma's garden was wonderful, full of sorghum, millet, and cassava.
But best of all were the bananas.
Although Grandma had many grandchildren, I secretly knew that I was her favourite. She invited me often to her house. She also told me little secrets.
But there was one secret she did not share with me: where she ripened bananas.

text:

But best of all were the bananas.
Although Grandma had many

translation: Bibi alikuwa na bustani nzuri iliyojaa mtama, ulezi na mihogo. Lakini kati ya mazao yote, alipenda zaidi ndizi. Japo bibi alikuwa na wajukuu wengi, nilikuja kubaini kuwa alikuwa ananipenda mimi zaidi ya wote. Mara nyingi alikuwa akinialika nyumbani kwake. Pia alikuwa ananiambia siri ndogo ndogo. Lakini kulikuwa na siri moja ambayo hakunishirikisha: alipokuwa anavundika ndizi.

text:
Sũsũ aĩna syana mbingĩ. Ĩndĩ katĩka
onthe, nyie na aamwaiya na
eetwiya kwa kĩmbithĩ nĩtwesĩ sũsũ
nũtwendete kũvĩta ala angĩ.
Nau nĩwe waĩ ĩlumaita ya sũsũ kwou
sũsũ atũkua kwa nzĩa ya mwanya.
Kwa ngelekany'o nĩwokaa mũsyĩ
kwitũ mavinda maingĩ. Ĩla ena nau
na mwaitũ nĩmathekaa mũno. Na
kĩngĩ nowatwĩtaa nyũmba kwake
mavinda maingĩ. Ĩũlũ wa syĩndũ
syonthe sũsũ nĩwatũtavasyaa
syĩmbithĩ syake ĩndĩ ve kĩmbithĩ
kĩmwe ũtatũtavya: vala waindĩa
maiũ make.
Mũthenya ũmwe nĩnonie kĩkavũ kya
malala kiĩtwe suanĩ nza wa nyũmba
ya sũsũ. Ĩla nakũlilye nĩ kyakĩ
nanengiwe ũsũngĩo ũmwe kana nĩ
kĩkavũ kya syama. Sũsũ anzũngĩa
ou nĩwendee kũalyũla kĩtembe kya
translation:
One day I saw a big straw basket placed in the sun outside Grandma's house. When I asked what it was for, the only answer I got was, "It's my magic basket."
Next to the basket, there were several banana leaves that Grandma turned from time to time. I was curious. "What are the leaves for, Grandma?" I asked. The only answer I got was, "They are my magic leaves."

text:

onthe, nyie na aamwaiya na
eetwiya kwa kĩmbithĩ nĩtwesĩ sũsũ
nũtwendete kũvĩta ala angĩ.
Nau nĩwe waĩ ĩlumaita ya sũsũ kwou

Mũthenya ũmwe nĩnonie kĩkavũ kya

ya sũsũ. Ĩla nakũlilye nĩ kyakĩ
