translation: Siku moja niliona tenga kubwa limeanikwa juani nje ya nyumba ya bibi. Nilipouliza lilikuwa la nini, jibu pekee nililopata lilikuwa, "Hilo ni tenga langu la maajabu." Pembeni mwa tenga lile kulikuwa na majani ya ndizi ambayo bibi alikuwa akiyageuza kila mara. Nilipatwa na shauku. "Bibi, hayo majani ni ya nini?" niliuliza. Jibu pekee nililopata lilikuwa, "Ni majani yangu ya maajabu."

text:
Vakuvĩ na kĩkavũ vaĩna mathangũ
ma maiũ wekalaa akwalyũla ĩvinda
kwa ĩvinda. "Mathangũ asu nĩmakĩ
sũsũ?" nĩnamũkũlilye na anzũngĩa
"aa nĩ mathangũ makwa ma kwĩka
syama." Mũminũkĩlyo, sũsũ
nĩwombĩanĩe maiũ onthe ala maĩ
nyekinĩ.
Kyaĩ kĩndũ kya kwendeesya kwona
sũsũ, ĩiũ ĩnene matũ ma maiũ na
kĩkavũ kya malala kĩnene. Onew'a
nĩnendaa kwĩloela nĩmanye ũndũ
sũsũ ũkũtũmĩa syĩndũ isu syonthe,
sũsũ nĩwandũmie ngeete kĩndũ
kuma vala ve mwaitũ.
translation:
It was so interesting watching Grandma, the bananas, the banana leaves and the big straw basket. But Grandma sent me off to my mother on an errand.
"Grandma, please, let me watch as you prepare..."
"Don't be stubborn, child, do as you are told," she insisted. I took off running.

text:
Vakuvĩ na kĩkavũ vaĩna mathangũ
ma maiũ wekalaa akwalyũla ĩvinda
kwa ĩvinda. "Mathangũ asu nĩmakĩ
sũsũ?" nĩnamũkũlilye na anzũngĩa
"aa nĩ mathangũ makwa ma kwĩka
syama." Mũminũkĩlyo, sũsũ
nĩwombĩanĩe maiũ onthe ala maĩ
nyekinĩ.
Kyaĩ kĩndũ kya kwendeesya kwona
sũsũ, ĩiũ ĩnene matũ ma maiũ na
kĩkavũ kya malala kĩnene. Onew'a
nĩnendaa kwĩloela nĩmanye ũndũ
sũsũ ũkũtũmĩa syĩndũ isu syonthe,
sũsũ nĩwandũmie ngeete kĩndũ
kuma vala ve mwaitũ.
translation: Nilikuwa na shauku kubwa kumwangalia bibi, ndizi, majani ya ndizi na tenga kubwa. Lakini bibi alinituma kwenda kwa mama. "Bibi, tafadhali naomba nitazame unavyoandaa..." "Usiwe msumbufu, fanya ulichoambiwa," alisisitiza. Nikaondoka nikikimbia.

text:
Ndililikana kĩndũ kĩu kyaĩ kyaũ.
Nĩnamwĩsũvie ngũmwĩa, "Sũsũ naku
eka nambe kwona wĩsovya...." "Eke
kwĩthĩwa kana keemu, ĩka ũndũ
watavwa." Sũsũ nĩwasũngĩie.
Nĩnaumie nĩsembete.
Nasyokethya nethĩie sũsũ ailye nza
wa nyũmba. "Sũsũ, kĩkavũ kĩva na
maiũ na...?" ĩndĩ ũsũngĩo ũla
nakwatie nĩkana, "Syĩvandũnĩ
vakwa va syama." Nĩnendaa
kũmanya vandũ vau va syama ĩndĩ
namũkũlya sũsũ nĩwendee
kwĩtwĩkĩthya kana ndakwĩw'a na
aendea kw'ina wathi. Nĩnakwie
ngoo.
translation:
When I returned, Grandma was sitting outside but with neither the basket nor the bananas.
"Grandma, where is the basket, where are all the bananas, and where..."
But the only answer I got was, "They are in my magic place." It was so disappointing!

text:
Ndililikana kĩndũ kĩu kyaĩ kyaũ.
Nĩnamwĩsũvie ngũmwĩa, "Sũsũ naku
eka nambe kwona wĩsovya...." "Eke
kwĩthĩwa kana keemu, ĩka ũndũ
watavwa." Sũsũ nĩwasũngĩie.
Nĩnaumie nĩsembete.
Nasyokethya nethĩie sũsũ ailye nza
wa nyũmba. "Sũsũ, kĩkavũ kĩva na
maiũ na...?" ĩndĩ ũsũngĩo ũla
nakwatie nĩkana, "Syĩvandũnĩ
vakwa va syama." Nĩnendaa
kũmanya vandũ vau va syama ĩndĩ
namũkũlya sũsũ nĩwendee
kwĩtwĩkĩthya kana ndakwĩw'a na
aendea kw'ina wathi. Nĩnakwie
ngoo.
translation: Niliporudi, bibi alikuwa amekaa nje, ila hakukuwa na tenga wala ndizi. "Bibi, tenga liko wapi, zile ndizi ziko wapi, na..." Jibu pekee nililopata lilikuwa, "Zipo kwenye eneo la maajabu." Ilikuwa inasikitisha.

text:
Matukũ elĩ mathela sũsũ aĩna mĩtũkĩ
ya kũthi mũkutano ndũanĩ.
Nĩwandũmie ngamwosee ndata
yake lumunĩ ya kũkoma. Ĩla
navingũie mwango wa lumu ĩsu
nĩnathokiswe nĩ muuke wa maiũ
makwĩw'a.
translation:
Two days later, Grandma sent me to fetch her walking stick from her bedroom.
As soon as I opened the door, I was welcomed by the strong smell of ripening bananas. In the inner room was grandma's big magic straw basket. It was well hidden by an old blanket. I lifted it and sniffed that glorious smell.

text:
Matukũ elĩ mathela sũsũ aĩna mĩtũkĩ
ya kũthi mũkutano ndũanĩ.
Nĩwandũmie ngamwosee ndata
yake lumunĩ ya kũkoma. Ĩla
navingũie mwango wa lumu ĩsu
nĩnathokiswe nĩ muuke wa maiũ
makwĩw'a.
translation: Siku mbili baadaye, bibi alinituma kwenda chumbani kwake kumletea mkongojo. Mara tu baada ya kufungua mlango, nilikaribishwa na harufu kali ya ndizi mbivu. Pembeni mwa chumba kulikuwa na tenga kubwa la maajabu la bibi. Lilikuwa limefichwa na blanketi la zamani. Nikaliinua na kunusa ile harufi nzuri.

text:
Lumunĩ ya nzĩnĩ ĩũsũĩte syĩndũ sya
sũsũ nĩvo vaĩna kĩla kĩkavũ kya sũsũ
kya syama kĩvĩthĩtwe nĩ ĩvula ĩkũũ.
Nĩnavwĩkũie ĩvula na muuke wa
maiũ wongelekela. Wasya wa sũsũ
nĩwandelemilye akwasya, "wĩka ata
we? Ngalatĩle ndata yakwa."
Nĩnamũsembeesye ndata na
angũlya, "nĩ kyaũ ukwetye kwenyea
kũtheka?" Ĩkũlyo yake nĩyatumiswe
ngũmanya kana nonendee
kwenyeea ĩtheka nũndũ wa
kũmanya vala vandũ va syama.
translation:
Grandma's voice startled me when she called, "What are you doing? Hurry up and bring me the stick."
I hurried out with her walking stick. "What are you smiling about?" Grandma asked.
Her question made me realise that I was still smiling at the discovery of her magic place.

text:
Lumunĩ ya nzĩnĩ ĩũsũĩte syĩndũ sya
sũsũ nĩvo vaĩna kĩla kĩkavũ kya sũsũ
kya syama kĩvĩthĩtwe nĩ ĩvula ĩkũũ.
Nĩnavwĩkũie ĩvula na muuke wa
maiũ wongelekela. Wasya wa sũsũ
nĩwandelemilye akwasya, "wĩka ata
we? Ngalatĩle ndata yakwa."
Nĩnamũsembeesye ndata na
angũlya, "nĩ kyaũ ukwetye kwenyea
kũtheka?" Ĩkũlyo yake nĩyatumiswe
ngũmanya kana nonendee
kwenyeea ĩtheka nũndũ wa
kũmanya vala vandũ va syama.
translation: Sauti ya bibi ilinishtua alipoita, "Unafanya nini? Fanya haraka niletee mkongojo." Nikaharakisha kwenda nje na mkongojo wake. "Unatabasamu nini?" bibi aliuliza. Swali lake likanifanya nigundue kuwa kumbe bado nilikuwa ninatabasamu baada ya kugundua eneo lake la maajabu.

text:
Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe sũsũ ooka
kũnena na mwaitũ nĩnosie
kamwanya ka kũsemba nyũmbanĩ
kwake ngasisye maiũ ĩngĩ. Vaĩ
kĩtembe kĩmwe kyew'ĩte vyũ.
Nĩnaumisye ĩiũ ĩmwe na navitha
ĩlindanĩ. Natũngĩa kĩla kĩndũ
nĩnasyokie nyũmba na naya ĩiũ
yakwa na mĩtũkĩ. Ndyaya ĩiũ yany'a
mũyo ũu ĩngĩ!
translation:
The following day when grandma came to visit my mother, I rushed to her house to check the bananas once more.
There was a bunch of very ripe ones. I picked one and hid it in my dress. After covering the basket again, I went behind the house and quickly ate it. It was the sweetest banana I had ever tasted.

text:
Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe sũsũ ooka
kũnena na mwaitũ nĩnosie
kamwanya ka kũsemba nyũmbanĩ
kwake ngasisye maiũ ĩngĩ. Vaĩ
kĩtembe kĩmwe kyew'ĩte vyũ.
Nĩnaumisye ĩiũ ĩmwe na navitha
ĩlindanĩ. Natũngĩa kĩla kĩndũ
nĩnasyokie nyũmba na naya ĩiũ
yakwa na mĩtũkĩ. Ndyaya ĩiũ yany'a
mũyo ũu ĩngĩ!
translation: Siku iliyofuata bibi alipokuja kumtembelea mama yangu, nikakimbilia nyumbani kwake kuangalia ndizi tena. Kulikuwa na vichane vya ndizi zilizoiva. Nikachukua ndizi moja na kuificha kwenye nguo yangu. Baada ya kufunika tenga tena, nikaenda nyuma ya nyumba na harakaharaka nikaila. Ilikuwa ni ndizi tamu ambayo sijawahi kula kamwe.

text:
Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe nĩnetelile sũsũ
athi kuuna mboka nasemba kũsisya
ala maiũ. Vakuvĩ onthe nĩmew'ĩte.
Ndyenamba kũmĩĩsya kũlea kwosa.
Nĩnosie ana na nekalata kuumala
nolwa kũvwĩka kĩkavũ.
translation:
The following day, when grandma was in the garden picking vegetables, I sneaked in and peered at the bananas.
Nearly all were ripe. I couldn't help taking a bunch of four.
As I tiptoed towards the door, I heard grandma coughing outside. I just managed to hide the bananas under my dress and walked past her.

text:
Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe nĩnetelile sũsũ
athi kuuna mboka nasemba kũsisya
ala maiũ. Vakuvĩ onthe nĩmew'ĩte.
Ndyenamba kũmĩĩsya kũlea kwosa.
Nĩnosie ana na nekalata kuumala
nolwa kũvwĩka kĩkavũ.
translation: Siku iliyofuata, bibi alipokuwa bustanini akichuma mboga, nikanyemelea ndani kuchungulia ndizi. Karibu zote zilikuwa zimeiva. Nikashindwa kujizuia nikachukua kichane cha ndizi nne. Nilipokuwa nanyata kuelekea mlangoni, nikamsikia bibi akikohoa nje. Nilifanikiwa kuzificha ndizi ndani ya nguo yangu na tukapishana bila ya kugundua.

text:
Nuumalĩte kavola na mĩthya ya
syaa sya maaũ Nĩnew'ie sũsũ
akũkoa vu nza. Nĩnatatie kũvitha
maiũ asu ĩlindanĩ. Namina kũya
nĩnasyokie na wethĩa sũsũ
ndanamanya mĩvango yakwa.
Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe waĩ wa
ndũnyũ. Sũsũ nĩwokĩlile tene nũndũ
kĩla wa ndũnyũ nĩwatwaa maiũ meu
na manga kũta. Ndyekalata kũthi
kũmũkethya mũthenya ũsu. Ĩndĩ
ndyenamba kũmwĩvitha kĩlungu
kyaasa.
translation:
The following day was market day. Grandma woke up early. She always took ripe bananas and cassava to sell at the market.
I did not hurry to visit her that day. But I could not avoid her for long.

text:
Nuumalĩte kavola na mĩthya ya
syaa sya maaũ Nĩnew'ie sũsũ
akũkoa vu nza. Nĩnatatie kũvitha
maiũ asu ĩlindanĩ. Namina kũya
nĩnasyokie na wethĩa sũsũ
ndanamanya mĩvango yakwa.
Mũthenya ũla watĩĩe waĩ wa
ndũnyũ. Sũsũ nĩwokĩlile tene nũndũ
kĩla wa ndũnyũ nĩwatwaa maiũ meu
na manga kũta. Ndyekalata kũthi
kũmũkethya mũthenya ũsu. Ĩndĩ
ndyenamba kũmwĩvitha kĩlungu
kyaasa.
translation: Siku iliyofuata ilikuwa siku ya gulio. Bibi aliamka asubuhi sana. Huwa anapeleka ndizi mbivu na mihogo kuuza gulioni. Siku hiyo sikuwa na haraka kwenda kumsalimia. Ila sikuweza kumkwepa kwa muda mrefu.

text:
Masaa ma wĩyoo ĩla netiwe nĩ
mwaitũ na nau na sũsũ nĩneesĩ kĩla
ngwĩtĩwa. Ũtukũ ngũkoma nĩneesĩ
kana ndikang'ea kĩndũ kya sũsũ
kana kya asyai makwa kana kya
mũndũ ũngĩ.
translation:
Later that evening I was called by my mother and father, and Grandma. I knew why.
That night as I lay down to sleep, I knew I could never steal again, not from grandma, not from my parents, and certainly not from anyone else.

text:
Masaa ma wĩyoo ĩla netiwe nĩ
mwaitũ na nau na sũsũ nĩneesĩ kĩla
ngwĩtĩwa. Ũtukũ ngũkoma nĩneesĩ
kana ndikang'ea kĩndũ kya sũsũ
kana kya asyai makwa kana kya
mũndũ ũngĩ.
translation: Jioni ile niliitwa na mama, baba na bibi. Nilijua kwanini. Usiku ule nilipokwenda kulala, nilijua siwezi kuiba tena. Siwezi kumwibia bibi, wazazi wangu na mtu yeyote yule.

text:
Ivinda ya tene kwai mundu wai na kila kindu – muunda munou, wai na ngombe, malondu na
mbui. Na aendee na ukua andeea kwithiwa na kimako, nundu ndai na kindu kimwe. Ndai
muka.
translation:
Once upon a time, there lived a man who had plenty of everything – a large fertile farm,
with cattle, sheep, and goats.
But, as he grew old, he grew sad, because one thing was missing.
He did not have a wife.

text:
Ivinda ya tene kwai mundu wai na kila kindu – muunda munou, wai na ngombe, malondu na
mbui. Na aendee na ukua andeea kwithiwa na kimako, nundu ndai na kindu kimwe. Ndai
muka.
translation:
Hapo zamani za kale, paliishi mzee aliyekuwa tajiri
wa kila kitu – shamba kubwa lenye rutuba, ng'ombe,
na mbuzi.
Lakini jinsi alivyokuwa akizeeka ndivyo alivyokuwa
akihuzunika kwani alikosa kitu fulani.
Hakuwa na mke.

text:
Aungamite ungu wa muti muthenya
umwe aukiwa ni ivindisya iseo.
Kethiwa ndona kiveti ai atonya
usovya kimwe?
translation:
Standing under a tree one day, he
had a brilliant idea.
If he couldn't find a wife, perhaps
he could make one?

text:
Aungamite ungu wa muti muthenya
umwe aukiwa ni ivindisya iseo.
Kethiwa ndona kiveti ai atonya
usovya kimwe?
translation:
Alipokuwa chini ya mti siku moja,
alipata wazo zuri sana.
Sasa kama hatapata mke, labda
atajitengenezea mmoja.

text:
Kwou ambia kuseuvya kiveti
kyanake kumana na uvonge wa
muti.
Ila waminie kuseuvya ivisa, akita
metho mayo na mavinguka.
Aivevea na yethiwa na thayu.
translation:
So he set to work to shape a
beautiful woman from a strong
branch of the tree. When he had
finished making the statue, he
touched her eyes, and they opened.
He blew gently on her, and she
came alive.

text:
Kwou ambia kuseuvya kiveti
kyanake kumana na uvonge wa
muti.
Ila waminie kuseuvya ivisa, akita
metho mayo na mavinguka.
Aivevea na yethiwa na thayu.
translation:
Sasa akaanza kazi ya kumchonga
mke kutoka kwa gogo la mti.
Wakati alikuwa amemaliza
kuchonga sanamu, aliigusa macho
ikaanza kuona.
Kisha aliipulizia pumzi ikawa hai.

text:
Kwaw'o kyai kiveti kyanake
utakyona vandu vangi.
Atulya ndu mbee wakyo to akikulya
ethiwe mume wakyo.
translation:
She was truly the most beautiful
woman he had ever seen.
He knelt before her, and asked her
to be his wife.

text:
Kwaw'o kyai kiveti kyanake
utakyona vandu vangi.
Atulya ndu mbee wakyo to akikulya
ethiwe mume wakyo.
translation:
Akawa mwanamke mrembo zaidi ya
wote aliokuwa ameona.
Alipiga magoti mbele yake na
kumwomba awe mkewe.

text:
Akinenga ngua nzeo, wanyua na
mbete ya mutwe kwonanya kyai
kiveti kitwae. Na akyakia nyumba
ya ndaka na nyeki ila yai vakuvi na
kitina kya muti vala kyaumie.
"Nikukulya kindu kimwe kwatei".
Atavya kiveti kyake.
"Ndukaatate utavya mundu vala
waumie".
translation:
He gave her a colourful apron,
beads, and a head ring, the sign of
a married woman. And he built her
a house with the mud and grass
that used to lie at the foot of her
trunk.
"Only one thing I beg of you," he
said to his wife. "Never tell anyone
where you come from."

text:
Akinenga ngua nzeo, wanyua na
mbete ya mutwe kwonanya kyai
kiveti kitwae. Na akyakia nyumba
ya ndaka na nyeki ila yai vakuvi na
kitina kya muti vala kyaumie.
"Nikukulya kindu kimwe kwatei".
Atavya kiveti kyake.
"Ndukaatate utavya mundu vala
waumie".
translation:
Yule mume alimvisha kimori,
shanga, na mkufu wa kichwani,
ishara kwamba alikuwa ameolewa.
Kisha alimjengea nyumba kwa
matope na nyasi.
"Ninakuomba kitu kimoja tu," jamaa
alisema. "Usimwambie mtu yeyote
mahali ulikotoka."

text:
Kwa kavinda kavuthu, aume ma
muika kuma utuini ungi mambiia
kuneena. "Mundu mukuu ta usu
atonya kwithiwa na kiveti kya muika
kyanake uu ata? Mavanga kukyosa
na kukitwaa kyuuni kyoo".
translation:
But before long, the young men
from a neighbouring village began
talking among themselves.
"How can such an old man have
such a beautiful young wife?"
So they decided to steal her and
take her to their own kraal.

text:
Kwa kavinda kavuthu, aume ma
muika kuma utuini ungi mambiia
kuneena. "Mundu mukuu ta usu
atonya kwithiwa na kiveti kya muika
kyanake uu ata? Mavanga kukyosa
na kukitwaa kyuuni kyoo".
translation:
Lakini kabla ya kipindi kirefu, vijana
kutoka kijiji jirani walianza kusema,
"Inawezekanaje mzee kama huyu
kumwoa msichana mrembo namna
hii!"
Basi wakaamua kumwiba msichana
yule wampeleke kijijini kwao.

text:
Mukuu uu niwethiwe na kyeva
muno.
Ndai atonya kwikala thayu atena
kiveti kiu.
Ateo avindisya yingi, "Ethiwa nina
kindu kyake ndyaile ni kumaka".
Kwou atuma mavui, kukimantha,
kukinia, na kumwetee o kindu kuma
kwakyo.
translation:
The old man was heartbroken. He
felt he could not live without her.
But then he thought, "Perhaps if I
have something of hers, I would not
feel so sad?"
So he sent his doves to find her, to
sing to her, and to bring back
something of hers to him.

text:
Mukuu uu niwethiwe na kyeva
muno.
Ndai atonya kwikala thayu atena
kiveti kiu.
Ateo avindisya yingi, "Ethiwa nina
kindu kyake ndyaile ni kumaka".
Kwou atuma mavui, kukimantha,
kukinia, na kumwetee o kindu kuma
kwakyo.
translation:
Mkewe alipoibiwa, mzee alihuzunika sana.
Alihisi kwamba hangeishi bila mkewe.
Lakini akafikiria, "Labda nikipata kitu chochote
kutoka kwake nitapata faraja."
Kwa hivyo, alituma njiwa wawili wakamtafute
mkewe, wamwimbie na wamletee kitu chochote
kutoka kwa mkewe.

text:
Ila makyonie, makiniie kwa
kithyomo kya nyunyi.
Kiveti kya muti kiveti kya muti,
Kiseo kitemoneka. Mwimiu
nututumie tumutungie ngua yaku.
translation:
When they found her, they sang to
her in the language of birds:
Tree woman, tree woman
More beautiful than any other
Your husband has sent us
To bring back your apron!

text:
Ila makyonie, makiniie kwa
kithyomo kya nyunyi.
Kiveti kya muti kiveti kya muti,
Kiseo kitemoneka. Mwimiu
nututumie tumutungie ngua yaku.
translation:
Walipomwona walimwimbia wimbo
mtamu katika lugha ya ndege:
Mke mti, mke mti,
Mrembo kuliko wote,
Tumetumwa na mumeo,
Tunakujia kimori,
Turudishe kwa mumeo,
Asije kukusahau.

text:
Kya manenga ngua yakyo, na mauluka iulu wa iima, mbusi, maendete kula kwi muume
wakyo.
Akwatie ngua yakyo vakuvi na uthyu na eewa muyo vanini.
translation:
She gave them her apron, and they flew over the hill, over the river, back to her husband.
He held the apron to his face, and was comforted for a little while.

text:
Kya manenga ngua yakyo, na mauluka iulu wa iima, mbusi, maendete kula kwi muume
wakyo.
Akwatie ngua yakyo vakuvi na uthyu na eewa muyo vanini.
translation:
Aliwapa Kimori chake wakapuruka, juu ya milima, juu ya mito, hadi wakarudi kwa mumewe.
Mzee alipokea kimori akakishika usoni mwake kwa furaha akapata faraja.

text:
Wendi wake uyathela mituki.
Niwatumiie mavui ingi makinie.
Kiveti kya muti, kiveti kya muti
kiseo kitemoneka, mwimiu
nututumie tumutungie mbete yaku
ya mutwe.
translation:
But his longing did not go away.
So again he sent his doves to sing
to her:
Tree woman, tree woman
More beautiful than any other
Your husband has sent us
To bring back your head ring!
And back they flew with the head
ring, the sign of a married woman.

text:
Wendi wake uyathela mituki.
Niwatumiie mavui ingi makinie.
Kiveti kya muti, kiveti kya muti
kiseo kitemoneka, mwimiu
nututumie tumutungie mbete yaku
ya mutwe.
translation:
Lakini hiyo faraja haikudumu muda mrefu:
Aliwatuma wale njiwa tena wakamwimbie mkewe:
Mke mti, mke mti,
Mrembo kuliko wote,
Tumetumwa na mumeo,
Tunakujia mkufu
Turudishe kwa mumeo,
Asije kukusahau.
Basi wakarudi tena wakibeba mkufu ambao ulikuwa
ishara ya mwanamke aliyeolewa.

text:
Akwete mbete ya mutwe
athumuuka nundu wa kiveti kyake
kikuasa kyuuni kya andu angi.
Kwa kavinda, eeta mavui make ingi.
Thyiuuthi kula kii mukaine, kiveti
kya muti kiveti kya muti kiseo
kitemoneka muimiu niatutumie
tumutungie thayu wake!
translation:
He held the head ring and sighed
for his wife, far away in the kraal of
other people.
After a while, he called his doves
again. He told them to go to her
and sing:
Tree woman, tree woman
More beautiful than any other
Your husband has sent us
To bring back your life!

text:
Akwete mbete ya mutwe
athumuuka nundu wa kiveti kyake
kikuasa kyuuni kya andu angi.
Kwa kavinda, eeta mavui make ingi.
Thyiuuthi kula kii mukaine, kiveti
kya muti kiveti kya muti kiseo
kitemoneka muimiu niatutumie
tumutungie thayu wake!
translation:
Aliuchukuwa ule mkufu wa kichwani akapata faraja
ya mke wake aliyekuwa katika kijiji cha watu
wengine.
Baada ya muda mfupi aliwaita njiwa tena,
akawatuma kwa mkewe tena wakamwimbie:
Mke mti, mke mti,
Mrembo kuliko wote,
Tumetumwa na mumeo,
Ataka maisha yako,
Turudishe kwa mumeo,
Asije kukusahau.

text:
Kwou mathi ivinda ya katatu.
Mavuila ituoni syakyo.
Mainite, kila isuni yatonga itho
mituki kyatwika ivisa. Maau na
moko mavaluka na mutwe. Na
kyavaluka muthangani.
translation:
So away they went the third time.
They perched on her shoulders. As
they sang, each bird pecked out an
eye.
Immediately she turned again into a
statue.
Her feet and arms fell away. Then
her head.
And she fell to the ground.

text:
Kwou mathi ivinda ya katatu.
Mavuila ituoni syakyo.
Mainite, kila isuni yatonga itho
mituki kyatwika ivisa. Maau na
moko mavaluka na mutwe. Na
kyavaluka muthangani.
translation:
kwa hivyo, walienda tena mara ya tatu wakatua
mabegani mwake.
Walipokuwa wakiimba, kila njiwa alikuwa akidona na
kumng'oa jicho.
Punde si punde, akageuka na kuwa sanamu.
Miguu na mikono yake ilidondoka.
Kichwa vilevile kilianguka. Akaanguka chini, pu!

text:
Kavola muume avingilitya kitina kya
muti usini.
Akyungamya na mii yakyo kiwuni.
Nundu wa isua na muthanga,
kyamesya matu ingi.
translation:
Her husband slowly rolled her
wooden trunk to the river.
He stood her up with her roots in
the water.
Nourished by sun and soil, she grew
leaves again.

text:
Kavola muume avingilitya kitina kya
muti usini.
Akyungamya na mii yakyo kiwuni.
Nundu wa isua na muthanga,
kyamesya matu ingi.
translation:
Mumewe alilisukuma lile gogo la
sanamu kwenye mto.
Akalisimamisha upande wa mizizi
ukiwa majini.
Na baada ya kupata maji na
kupigwa na miale ya jua lile gogo
liliota majani tena kama zamani.

text:
Na ukungi wikwo matu nimaumasya
wasya.
Otondu kiveti kikaa kikwenda
muume.
translation:
And when the wind blows, the
leaves sigh.
Just as a woman does when she
longs for her husband.

text:
Na ukungi wikwo matu nimaumasya
wasya.
Otondu kiveti kikaa kikwenda
muume.
translation:
Na wakati upepo uvumapo,majani
yake hushusha pumzi kama vile
mwanamke hushusha pumzi
anapotamani kumwona mumewe.

text:
Mbui,Ngiti na Ng'ombe
mai anyanyae
anene.Muthenyia umwe
maendie kyalo na ngali.
translation:
Sakima lived with his parents and his four year old sister.
They lived on a rich man's land.
Their grass-thatched hut was at the end of a row of trees.

text:
Mbui,Ngiti na Ng'ombe
mai anyanyae
anene.Muthenyia umwe
maendie kyalo na ngali.
translation: Sakima aliishi na wazazi wake na dada yake wa miaka minne. Waliishi katika shamba la mtu tajiri. Nyumba yao ya nyasi ilikuwa mwisho wa safu ya miti iliyopendeza.

text:
Mavika kwisho wa
kyaloi,Ndeleva amea
maive tikiti.Ng'ombe
aiva tikiti wake.
translation:
When Sakima was three years old, he fell sick and lost his sight.
Sakima was a talented boy.

text:
Mavika kwisho wa
kyaloi,Ndeleva amea
maive tikiti.Ng'ombe
aiva tikiti wake.
translation: Sakima alipokuwa na umri wa miaka mitatu, aliugua na kupoteza uwezo wa kuona. Hata hivyo, Sakima alikuwa mvulana mwenye kipaji.

text:
Ngiti aiva tikiti
umwingaingi,nundu
ndaii na mbesa ila
syailite.
translation:
Sakima did many things that other six year old boys did not do.
For example, he could sit with older members of the village and discuss important matters.

text:
Ngiti aiva tikiti
umwingaingi,nundu
ndaii na mbesa ila
syailite.
translation: Sakima alitenda mambo mengi ambayo wavulana wengine wa umri wake hawakufanya. Kwa mfano, angeketi na watu wazima na kujadili mambo muhimu.

text:
Ndeleva akwenda
utungia Ngiti mbesa sya
uluui,Mbui aumela
asembete ataivite
kindu!
translation:
The parents of Sakima worked at the rich man's house.
They left home early in the morning and returned late in the evening.
Sakima was left with his little sister.

text:
Ndeleva akwenda
utungia Ngiti mbesa sya
uluui,Mbui aumela
asembete ataivite
kindu!
translation: Wazazi wa Sakima walifanya kazi katika nyumba ya yule tajiri. Walitoka nyumbani asubuhi na mapema na kurudi jioni. Sakima aliachwa na dada yake.

text:
Ndeleva athata
muno.Atwaa ngali
atanatungia Ngiti
mbesa sya yuulu.
translation:
Sakima loved to sing songs.
One day his mother asked him, "Where do you learn these songs from, Sakima?"

text:
Ndeleva athata
muno.Atwaa ngali
atanatungia Ngiti
mbesa sya yuulu.
translation: Sakima alipenda kuimba nyimbo. Siku moja mama yake alimuuliza, "Sakima, unajifunza nyimbo hizi kutoka wapi?"

text:
Ni kwio kitumi ona
umunze Ngiti usembea
ngali
akunikile nzini aimaza
Ndeleva ula
utamutungia mbesa
syake sya yuulu.
translation: Sakima answered, "They just come, mother. I hear them in my head and then I sing."

text:
Ni kwio kitumi ona
umunze Ngiti usembea
ngali
akunikile nzini aimaza
Ndeleva ula
utamutungia mbesa
syake sya yuulu.
translation: Sakima alimjibu, "Nazisikia akilini mwangu kisha naziimba."

text:
Mbui nake asembaa
aitoloka muumo wa
ngali.Ethia aikia
ndakakwatwe nundu wa
ulea iva tikiti wake.
translation:
Sakima liked to sing for his little sister, especially, if she felt hungry.
His sister would listen to him singing his favourite song.
She would sway to the soothing tune.

text:
Mbui nake asembaa
aitoloka muumo wa
ngali.Ethia aikia
ndakakwatwe nundu wa
ulea iva tikiti wake.
translation: Sakima alipenda kumwimbia mdogo wake hasa akihisi njaa. Dada yake alimsikiliza na kucheza.

text:
Na Ng'ombe
ndatelemaa ngali
yukite.Ng'ombe osaa
ivinda yake kukilanilia
nzia nundu niwaivie
tikiti wake wonze!
translation:
"Can you sing it again and again, Sakima," his sister would beg him.
Sakima would accept and sing it over and over again.

text:
Na Ng'ombe
ndatelemaa ngali
yukite.Ng'ombe osaa
ivinda yake kukilanilia
nzia nundu niwaivie
tikiti wake wonze!
translation: "Naomba uimbe tena na tena, Sakima," mdogo wake alimsihi. Sakima alikubali na kuimba mara nyingine.

text: Kyai kiwiyoo kivyu kya wathanthatu mwei wa ikumi na ili. Kila umwe ai muthatu. "Bontle na Mpho na Leroto, umalai muthauke" Mme atutavya. "Ndi kumwenda vakuvi nakwa."
translation: It was a very hot Saturday afternoon in December.

text: Kyai kiwiyoo kivyu kya wathanthatu mwei wa ikumi na ili. Kila umwe ai muthatu. "Bontle na Mpho na Leroto, umalai muthauke" Mme atutavya. "Ndi kumwenda vakuvi nakwa."
translation:
Ilikuwa Jumamosi moja
iliyokuwa na joto jingi sana
katika mwezi wa Desemba.
Kila mtu alikuwa amenuna.
"Bontle na Mpho na Lerato,
nendeni nje mcheze!" Mama
alitwambia.
"Siwataki miguuni mwangu."

text: Twaumaaluka tusembete. "Tuthii usini" Loreto atutavya. "Vau ni vathithangu." "Indi Mme atwia twikativie usini" Bontle atutavya " Tuyitivia" Leroto asungia. "Tuthauke munyini vakuvi na kiwu."
translation: "Bontle and Mpho and Lerato, go out and play!" Mme said to us. "I don't want you under my feet." We ran out of the house.

text: Twaumaaluka tusembete. "Tuthii usini" Loreto atutavya. "Vau ni vathithangu." "Indi Mme atwia twikativie usini" Bontle atutavya " Tuyitivia" Leroto asungia. "Tuthauke munyini vakuvi na kiwu."
translation:
Tulikimbia nje ya nyumba.
"Twendeni mtoni," Lerato
alisema. "Huko ni baridi."
"Lakini mama alitukataza
kuogelea mtoni," alisema
Bontle.
"Hatutaogelea," alijibu Lerato.
"Tutachezea tu kwenye kivuli
karibu na maji,"

text: Ateo ithau ya 'libeke' ni ivyu ona ethiwa wi ungu wa miti vakuvi na usi. Mbee twaumya syaatu. Indi twai o avyu. Twaumya sati na sikati. Indi twai o avayu.
translation: "Let's go to the river," Lerato said. "It's cooler there." "But Mme told us not to swim in the river," said Bontle. "We won't swim," answered Lerato. "We'll just play in the shade next to the water."

text: Ateo ithau ya 'libeke' ni ivyu ona ethiwa wi ungu wa miti vakuvi na usi. Mbee twaumya syaatu. Indi twai o avyu. Twaumya sati na sikati. Indi twai o avayu.
translation:
Lakini kucheza 'kati' ni kazi ya
joto hata kama uko chini ya miti
karibu na mto.
Kwanza tulivua viatu vyetu.
Lakini tulikuwa bado tunahisi
joto.
Kisha tulivua sketi zetu na
mashati.
Lakini tulikuwa bado tunahisi
joto.

text: Twekia maau usini mathithe. Na twombangana kiwu. Mituki twamena kiwu.
translation: But playing libeke is hot work, even when you're under the trees next to the river. First we took off our shoes. But we were still hot. Then we took off our shirts and skirts. But we were still hot.

text: Twekia maau usini mathithe. Na twombangana kiwu. Mituki twamena kiwu.
translation:
Tuliweka miguu yetu ndani ya
mto kuifanya iwe baridi.
Kisha tulirushiana maji.
Punde kidogo tulikuwa tumeloa
maji.

text: "Inywi nenyu! Tutiviei" Asya Mpho. "Mme ndakamanya" Twativia na twativia nginya twolwa ni ivinda.
translation: We put our feet in the river to cool off. Then we splashed each other. Soon we were soaked with water.

text: "Inywi nenyu! Tutiviei" Asya Mpho. "Mme ndakamanya" Twativia na twativia nginya twolwa ni ivinda.
translation:
"Ah njoo! Hebu tuogelee,"
alisema Mpho. "Mama hatawahi
jua."
Tuliogelea kwa muda mrefu na
kusahau kuwa saa zilikuwa
zikiendelea.

text: Sua yambiia kuthua na twambiia kwiwa mbevo ngua situ syaiva?
translation: "Oh come on! Let's swim," said Mpho. "Mme will never know." We swam and swam and forgot about the time.

text: Sua yambiia kuthua na twambiia kwiwa mbevo ngua situ syaiva?
translation:
Jua lilianza kutua, na tulihisi
baridi.
Lakini je, nguo zetu zilikuwa
wapi?

text: Twamantha ungu wa miti. Twamantha kithekani Twamantha kila vandu.
translation: The sun started to go down, and the day began to cool. Where were our clothes?

text: Twamantha ungu wa miti. Twamantha kithekani Twamantha kila vandu.
translation:
Tuliangalia chini ya miti.
Tuliangalia juu ya vichaka.
Tuliangalia kila mahali.

text: Ateo vai ngombe syai vakuvi na usi sikuya nyeki syai muyo. Bontle asisya iulu! " Sisya ngombe iya! Yumite kyau? "Iya ilaa itune" Lerato asya."
translation: We looked under the trees. We looked on the bushes. We looked everywhere.

text: Ateo vai ngombe syai vakuvi na usi sikuya nyeki syai muyo. Bontle asisya iulu! " Sisya ngombe iya! Yumite kyau? "Iya ilaa itune" Lerato asya."
translation:
Ng'ombe walikuwa wakifurahia
nyasi tamu karibu na mto.
Bontle aliangalia juu, "Ona yule
ng'ombe! Nini kilicho mdomoni
mwake?"
"Anakula ua jekundu," Lerato
alisema.

text: "Ti ilaa itune" Mpho atulya wasya. "Ni sati yaku" Twasisya ngombe ingi yutanyuka kindu ki mbuluu. "Isu ni skati yakwa" Bontle atulya wasya.
translation: There were some cows near the river, enjoying the sweet grass. Bontle looked up, "Look at that cow! What's in her mouth?" "She's eating a red flower," said Lerato. "It's not a red flower," shouted Mpho. "It's your shirt!"

text: "Ti ilaa itune" Mpho atulya wasya. "Ni sati yaku" Twasisya ngombe ingi yutanyuka kindu ki mbuluu. "Isu ni skati yakwa" Bontle atulya wasya.
translation:
"Sio ua jekundu," Mpho alipiga
kelele. "Ni shati lako!"
Tulimwangalia ng'ombe
mwingine.
Alikuwa anakula kitu cha
kisamwati.

text:
Vau tene, vai iimu ika.
Muthenya umwe yiitembea vakuvi
na iia niyonie twilitu tutatu tunini.
Yatukulya "nuu kati wenyu
wendetwe ni asyai onthe.
translation:
Once upon a time there was a
female giant.
As she was walking near the lake
one day, she found three little girls.
She asked them, "Who among you
is loved by both parents?"

text:

wendetwe ni asyai onthe.
translation:
Hapo zamani za kale paliondokea
jitu la kike. Lilipokuwa likitembea
kandokando mwa ziwa liliwaona
wasichana watatu.
Likawauliza, "Ni nani kati yenu
anayependwa na wazazi wote
wawili?"

text:
Kelitu kamwe kasya "mwaitu
ambendete muno"
Kangi kasya "Tata ambendete
muno"
Kakatatu kasya, "nendetwe ni asyai
onthe".
translation:
One of the girls said, "My mother
loves me most."
Another said, "My father loves me
most."
But the third one said, "I am loved
by both parents."

text:
Kelitu kamwe kasya "mwaitu

Kakatatu kasya, "nendetwe ni asyai

Msichana wa kwanza akasema,
"Mamangu hunipenda zaidi."
Mwingine akasema, "Babangu
hunipenda zaidi."
Lakini wa tatu akasema,
"Ninapendwa na wazazi wote
sawa."

text:
Iimu yeya kelitu kala kendetwe ni
asyai onthe kayaikye ngu mwongo.
Kwoou kelitu katiia iimu.
translation:
The giant then asked the girl loved
by both parents to help her put a
load of firewood on her back.
So the girl followed the giant.

text:
Iimu yeya kelitu kala kendetwe ni

Kisha jitu likamwambia msichana
anayependwa na wazazi wote
alifuate akalisaidie kuinua tita la
kuni mgongoni. Kwa hivyo,
msichana huyo alilifuata jitu.

text:
Maendanga vanini, kelitu kakulya
iimu "ngu syaku syiva" Iimu
yasungia, "vakuvi na mii iyaa".
translation:
After going for some distance, the
girl asked the giant, "Where is your
firewood?"
The giant replied, "It is near those
trees over there!"

text:
Maendanga vanini, kelitu kakulya

translation:
Baada ya kutembea kidogo,
msichana akaliuliza jitu, "Wapi kuni
zako?"
Jitu likajibu, "Ziko karibu na ile miti,
pale!"

text:
Mavika mitini, kelitu kakulya ingi "
ngu syaku syiva?" Iimu yasungia
kana mangie uvika.
translation:
When they reached the trees, the
girl asked again, "Where is your
firewood?"
The giant answered, "Not far now!"

Mavika mitini, kelitu kakulya ingi "

translation:
Walipofika kwenye miti hiyo,
msichana akauliza jitu tena, "Wapi
kuni zako?"
Jitu likajibu, "Haziko mbali sasa."

Maenda na makomana na mundu

ketewa ata" Iimu yasya "Ketawa
muvuko unenaa".
translation:
They walked on and met a man.
He asked the giant, "What is the
name of your child?"
The giant replied, "She is called the
'talking bag'."

na mwanamume.
Mwanamume akaliuliza jitu, "Huyu
mtoto wako anaitwaje?" Jitu likajibu,
"Anaitwa Mfuko Uzunguzao."

Oh! My mother, whom I love,

drink milk!"

sang, he rescued her and took her
back to her parents.
The story ends there!

translation:

spider called Anansi.

food. Instead, he used to visit his
friends and eat the delicious food
they had cooked.

"Greens!" he said excitedly.

Rabbit. "You can help me with the
washing up in the mean time."
"Sorry, I have things to do. I'll come
back later," said Anansi.

one end around my leg and one end
to your pot. When the greens are
ready, pull on the web string and I'll
come right away."
So Anansi tied the web to the pot,
and walked on.

Maĩlĩte kũthũkũma wĩa
woo w'onthe ũtukũ.
Nũndũ mĩĩ yoo yaseovetw'e na mũvũa!
translation:
They had to do all their
work during the night.
Because they were made of wax!

text:
Maĩlĩte kũthũkũma wĩa
woo w'onthe ũtukũ.
Nũndũ mĩĩ yoo yaseovetw'e na mũvũa!
translation: Walifanya kazi zao zote usiku. Hii ni kwa sababu walikuwa wameumbwa kwa nta.

text:
Ĩndĩ mwana ũmwe aĩ na
mea ma kũthi nza
kwĩanĩkĩa kyeni kya sua.
translation:
But one of the boys
longed to go out in the
sunlight.

text:
Ĩndĩ mwana ũmwe aĩ na
mea ma kũthi nza
kwĩanĩkĩa kyeni kya sua.
translation: Lakini, kijana mmoja alitamani kwenda nje wakati wa mchana.

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe
nĩwethĩiw'e na mea asu
ma kũthi nza muno.
Ĩndĩ aamwanainya
nĩmamũkanisye...
translation:
One day the longing
was too strong. His
brothers warned him...

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe
nĩwethĩiw'e na mea asu
ma kũthi nza muno.
Ĩndĩ aamwanainya
nĩmamũkanisye...
translation: Siku moja tamaa ya kwenda nje ikazidi. Wenzake wakamwonya asiende juani. Lakini, hakusikia.

text:
Ũũi! Mwana ũsu
ndaatetheka.
Nĩwanyinyũkie nũndũ
wa ũvyuvu wa sua.
translation:
But it was too late!
He melted in the hot
sun.

text:
Ũũi! Mwana ũsu
ndaatetheka.
Nĩwanyinyũkie nũndũ
wa ũvyuvu wa sua.
translation: Aliyeyuka kwa sababu joto lilikuwa kali.

text:
Syana sya mũvũa
nĩsyakwatiwe ni kyeva
nũndũ wa kwona
mwanaainya
ainyinyuka.
translation:
The wax children were
so sad to see their
brother melting away.

text:
Syana sya mũvũa
nĩsyakwatiwe ni kyeva
nũndũ wa kwona
mwanaainya
ainyinyuka.
translation: Watoto wa nta walihuzunika walipoona kaka yao akiyeyuka.

text:
Ĩndĩ nĩmethĩiw'e na
mũvango. Nĩmosie
mũndo wa mũvũa ula
wanyinyukie maseovya
kasũni.
translation:
But they made a plan.
They shaped the lump
of melted wax into a
bird.

text:
Ĩndĩ nĩmethĩiw'e na
mũvango. Nĩmosie
mũndo wa mũvũa ula
wanyinyukie maseovya
kasũni.
translation: Wakapanga jambo fulani. Walichukua nta iliyoyeyuka wakatengeza ndege.

text:
Nĩmosie mwanaainya
kasũni mamũlĩsya ĩũlu
wa kĩĩma kĩtũlu.
translation:
They took their bird
brother up to a high
mountain.

text:
Nĩmosie mwanaainya
kasũni mamũlĩsya ĩũlu
wa kĩĩma kĩtũlu.
translation: Wakamweka ndege huyo juu ya mlima mrefu.

text:
Na sua ĩkuuma
nĩwolũkile athi kũu
akwina kyeninĩ kya
kĩoko.
translation:
And as the sun rose, he
flew away singing into
the morning light.

text:
Na sua ĩkuuma
nĩwolũkile athi kũu
akwina kyeninĩ kya
kĩoko.
translation: Jua lilipochomoza asubuhi, akapeperuka akiimba kwa furaha.

text:
Sipho aendete tauni na
mwiitu yinya.
translation:
Sipho goes to town with
his sister.

extra.text_by: Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla, Zanele Buthelezi

text:
Mwiitu yinya wake
asyaisye ngua ndukani.
Sipho niuboikie.
translation:
His sister is looking at
the clothes in shops.
Sipho is bored.

extra.text_by: Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla, Zanele Buthelezi

text:
Sipho asyaise kindu
wivata nakyo.
translation:
Sipho sees something
he likes.

extra.text_by: Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla, Zanele Buthelezi

text: Siatu ni kuteewa.
translation: The shoes are on sale.

extra.text_by: Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla, Zanele Buthelezi

text: Aelile syonthe.
translation: He tries them all on.

extra.text_by: Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla, Zanele Buthelezi

text:
Mwiitu inyia wake
amuyiye siatu sya
muvila .
translation:
His sister buys him
soccer shoes.

extra.text_by: Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla, Zanele Buthelezi

text:
Kwa vaati nzeo alikie
kiwanzani kya mauu
isaani! Ekite siatu syake
sya muvila wa mauu.
translation:
Why are they in such a
hurry to get home?

extra.text_by: Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla, Zanele Buthelezi

text:
Kwa ivinda iasa, Olokwango
aungamite akenyesya itheka
katikati wa uii wa kwene. Kuma
Malong'ola eli ngali syonthe ili,
vaumite mbusi ila syakomanite
miandani kuseuvya usi. Usi wa
Temu wavitilite uini wa Kweni
ukilitye ki. Kiwu kyaw'o kyai
kinengo kwa ng'ombe, matunda na
mbui sya utuini ovamwe na Nzia ila
yekalaa uini usu.
translation:
For ages, Olokwango hill stood smiling at the middle
of Kwere plains. From the two dimples on its side
came springs which converged downhill to form a
river. River Temu meandered silently across the
Kwere plains. Its waters were a gift to the sheep and
goats of the area as well as the deer that dwelt in the
plains.

text:
Kwa ivinda iasa, Olokwango
aungamite akenyesya itheka
katikati wa uii wa kwene. Kuma
Malong'ola eli ngali syonthe ili,
vaumite mbusi ila syakomanite
miandani kuseuvya usi. Usi wa
Temu wavitilite uini wa Kweni
ukilitye ki. Kiwu kyaw'o kyai
kinengo kwa ng'ombe, matunda na
mbui sya utuini ovamwe na Nzia ila
yekalaa uini usu.
translation:
Kwa muda mrefu mlima wa
Olokwango ulisimama ukitabasamu
katikati ya sehemu Tambarare ya
Kwere.
Kutoka kwa vibonyeo viwili
vilivyokuwa pembeni mwa mlima
huo, kulitoka vijito vilivyokaribiana
na kutengeza mto.

text:
Maundu maendee nesa muvaka ila
Matata watwikie mutui. Aisye nzia
niseuvwe isilite kiimani nikana
alisae kiimani vate thina wa
uvingilita mbika nthi kavola. Kiima
kya Olokwango nikyathatie muno,
nundu wa kwanangwa kwa
king'ewa kyake ateo kyaumisya.
translation:
Things were all well until Matata became headman.
He ordered a path to be cleared from the top of the
hill to the foot so that he could climb uphill easily
and roll gently down to the foot. Olokwango hill was
angry with the damage to his beard, but he was
patient.

text:
Maundu maendee nesa muvaka ila
Matata watwikie mutui. Aisye nzia
niseuvwe isilite kiimani nikana
alisae kiimani vate thina wa
uvingilita mbika nthi kavola. Kiima
kya Olokwango nikyathatie muno,
nundu wa kwanangwa kwa
king'ewa kyake ateo kyaumisya.
translation:
Mambo yalikuwa swari hadi Matata
alipokuwa mkuu wa mahali hapo.
Alilazimisha njia itengenezwe
kutoka juu ya mlima hadi chini yake
ili aweze kupanda kwa urahis na
kujifiringisha chini ya mlima.
Mlima wa Olokwango ulikasirika na
uharibifu uliofanywa lakini alikuwa
mvumilivu.

text:
Muthia wa kyumwa, syana sya
Matata na anyangae moo nimalisaa
kiimani kuthauka. Masembaa kila
vandu, maitulanga mbonge sya
miti, makyakany'a miaki na kumitia
yakene.
translation:
During the weekend, Matata's children and their
friends would climb uphill to play.
They would run all over the place, breaking twigs
and branches, lighting fires for their games, which
they would later leave burning.

text:
Muthia wa kyumwa, syana sya
Matata na anyangae moo nimalisaa
kiimani kuthauka. Masembaa kila
vandu, maitulanga mbonge sya
miti, makyakany'a miaki na kumitia
yakene.
translation:
Mwishoni mwa wiki, watoto wa
Matata na marafiki zao
wangepanda mlimani kucheza.
Wangekimbia kila mahali huku
wakivunja vijiti na matawi,
wakiasha mioto kwa michezo yao
ambayo baadaye, waliacha ikiwaka.

text:
Kwa ivinda Olokwango anoa. Kavola
aeka kukenyeesya itheka.
Malong'ola maendeea na unyiva na
uthyu wake waendeea na
ukunzana. Mwisio ila mbusi ili
syang'ala. Nguka sya usi wa Temu
syasianisya kwa kimako. Nzia ila
syai uini syathama nundu vayai
nyeki ndaasa, ithaukia na vandu
vavinyu vaukoma. Ng'ombe, mbui
na malondu syamosa vyu. Kila
umwe eew'a kimako kya kiima kya
Olokwongo.
translation:
Over time, Olokwango lost patience. The dimples
became smaller and smaller as his face turned into
ugly wrinkles.
At last the springs were no more. The deer in the
plains migrated because there was no more the tall
green grass to play in. The sheep and goats grew
thinner and thinner.
Everyone felt the sadness of Olokwango hill.

text:
Kwa ivinda Olokwango anoa. Kavola
aeka kukenyeesya itheka.
Malong'ola maendeea na unyiva na
uthyu wake waendeea na
ukunzana. Mwisio ila mbusi ili
syang'ala. Nguka sya usi wa Temu
syasianisya kwa kimako. Nzia ila
syai uini syathama nundu vayai
nyeki ndaasa, ithaukia na vandu
vavinyu vaukoma. Ng'ombe, mbui
na malondu syamosa vyu. Kila
umwe eew'a kimako kya kiima kya
Olokwongo.
translation:
Kwa muda mrefu, Olokwango
alipoteza ule uvumilivu. Tabasamu
yake nzuri ilififia. Vibonyeo
viliendelea kuwa vidogo jinsi uso
wake uligeuka na kuwa na sura
mbaya ya mikunjo.
Mwishowe, vijito havikuwa tena.
Kingo za Mto Temu zilibaki
zikikaziana macho kwa huzuni.
Paa wa sehemu walihama kwani
hapakuwa tena na zile nyasi ndefu
za kijani walizochezea ndani, wala
godoro nyororo kulala juu yake.
Mifugo, mbuzi na kondoo walikonda
na kukondeana.
Kila mtu alihisi huzuni wa mlima wa
Olokwango.

text:
Andu ma Kwere nimamanyie kana ve kindu kikwenda
kwikwa. Nimakwatanie na maumya Matata kivilani.
Vandu vake manyuva Baraka ula mituki waisye kila
mundu navande ilaa manenge Olokwongo ndaia.
Baraka na andu make maseuvya sikuku na maete
mithinzio ya miti ya maana kwa Olokwongo.
translation:
The people of Kwere realized that something needed
to be done.
They joined hands and overthrew Matata the
headman.
In his place they appointed Baraka who immediately
ordered everyone to plant a flower to honour
Olokwango. Baraka and his people held ceremonies
and brought gifts of pine, cedar, and cypress for
Olokwango.

text:
Andu ma Kwere nimamanyie kana ve kindu kikwenda
kwikwa. Nimakwatanie na maumya Matata kivilani.
Vandu vake manyuva Baraka ula mituki waisye kila
mundu navande ilaa manenge Olokwongo ndaia.
Baraka na andu make maseuvya sikuku na maete
mithinzio ya miti ya maana kwa Olokwongo.
translation:
Watu wa Kwere waligundua kwamba walitakiwa
kuchukuwa hatua. Waliungana na kumpindua Matata
mkuu wao.
Pahali pake walimweka Baraka ambaye aliamrisha
kila mtu kupanda ua kuonyesha heshima kwa
Olokwango. Baraka na watu wake walifanya sherehe
na kumtolea Olokwango zawadi za msonobari,
mwerezi, na muhuhu.
Hakuna aliyetembea juu ya mlima tena, na nyasi
zilipata nafasi ya kumea na kuwa ndefu tena.
Kidogo kidogo tabasamu iliyokuwa usoni mwa mlima
wa Olokwango ilipanuka zaidi na vibonyeo vikarefuka
zaidi.

text:
Vai mundu watenbeelaa kiimani kiu
na nyeki yamea yingi. Kwa kavola
itheka ya kiima kya Olokwongo
yaingiva na malongola malikanga.
Kuma malongolani asu mbusi
syaumila ingi. Usi wa Temu
wathayuuka. Mbii syatwika sya
kisunzuni nundu wa miti na nyeki.
Nzia syambiia kusembasemba ingi
ku nyekini. Ng'ombe, mbui, na
malondu syathumua munyini wa
miti.
translation:
No one walked on the hill any longer, and the grass
had a chance to grow tall once again.
Gradually the smile on the face of Olokwango hill
grew broader and the dimples deeper. Out of the
dimples the springs ran again. River Temu was
rejuvenated. The plains became greener than ever
before. The deer galloped happily once more across
the grass.

text:
Vai mundu watenbeelaa kiimani kiu
na nyeki yamea yingi. Kwa kavola
itheka ya kiima kya Olokwongo
yaingiva na malongola malikanga.
Kuma malongolani asu mbusi
syaumila ingi. Usi wa Temu
wathayuuka. Mbii syatwika sya
kisunzuni nundu wa miti na nyeki.
Nzia syambiia kusembasemba ingi
ku nyekini. Ng'ombe, mbui, na
malondu syathumua munyini wa
miti.
translation:
Kutoka kwenye vibonyeo vijito
vilitiririka tena.
Mto Temu ulifufuliwa. Sehemu
tambarare ziligeuka kijani zaidi ya
hapo awali.
Paa walikimbia tena kwa furaha
kutoka upande mmoja hadi
mwingine wa nyasi.

text:
"Ikala thayu mwasa Baraka, ikala
thayu mwasa Baraka" andu ma
Kwere maina. "Ikala thayu mwasa
Olokwongo" Baraka na andu masya.
"Syana syenyu na syana sya syana
syoo na nzukulu syoo nisyunenge
ndaia kila ivinda.
translation:
"Long live Baraka, long live Baraka," the people of
Kwere sang.
"Long live, Olokwango," said Baraka and his people.
"May our children and children's children forever
respect you."

text:
"Ikala thayu mwasa Baraka, ikala
thayu mwasa Baraka" andu ma
Kwere maina. "Ikala thayu mwasa
Olokwongo" Baraka na andu masya.
"Syana syenyu na syana sya syana
syoo na nzukulu syoo nisyunenge
ndaia kila ivinda.
translation:
"Maisha marefu, Baraka! Maisha
marefu, Baraka!" watu wa Kwere
waliimba.
"Maisha marefu,
Olokwango,"Baraka na watu wake
walisema. "Heri watoto wetu na
watoto wa watoto wao
wakuheshima daima."

text:
Kayanga ekalile na asyai make
nginya metwa emĩaka ĩkũmi.
translation:
Khayanga lived with her parents
happily until they died when she
was ten years old.

text:
Kayanga ekalile na asyai make
nginya metwa emĩaka ĩkũmi.
translation:
Khayanga aliishi na wazazi wake
kwa furaha hadi siku walipofariki
akiwa na miaka kumi.

text:
Kĩveti kĩmwe kya mũkonyo woo
kyetawa Losa nĩkyamwosie kyathi
kwĩkala nake mũsyĩ kwakyo.
Losa aĩngya na mũkũũ ĩndĩ
aĩmũthingu.
translation:
Khayanga was taken in by Rosa, a
distant relative.
Rosa was kind to Khayanga, but she
was old, frail and poor.

text:
Kĩveti kĩmwe kya mũkonyo woo
kyetawa Losa nĩkyamwosie kyathi
kwĩkala nake mũsyĩ kwakyo.
Losa aĩngya na mũkũũ ĩndĩ
aĩmũthingu.
translation:
Khayanga alichukuliwa ili kutunzwa
na mama mmoja wa ukoo wake
aliyeitwa Rosa.
Rosa alikuwa mkarimu kwa
Khayanga. Lakini mama huyu
alikuwa mzee, maskini na alikuwa
amedhoofika sana.

text:
Kayanga mavinda maingĩ nĩwendaa
tũvulĩnĩ twa asyai make kũmatavya
mathĩna make.
translation:
Khayanga often visited her parents'
graves to tell them of her misery.

text:
Kayanga mavinda maingĩ nĩwendaa
tũvulĩnĩ twa asyai make kũmatavya
mathĩna make.
translation:
Khayanga alitembelea makaburi ya
wazazi wake mara kwa mara ili
kuwaeleza matatizo yake.

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe ĩla Kayanga
wendie kwona tũvulĩ nĩwanengiwe
mũthĩnzĩo mũseo wa kĩkuu kya
mwanya Kyaumĩlile tũvulĩnĩ twa
asyai make.
translation:
One day when she visited, she
received a gift. It was a very special
Gourd which appeared from her
parents' graves.

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe ĩla Kayanga
wendie kwona tũvulĩ nĩwanengiwe
mũthĩnzĩo mũseo wa kĩkuu kya
mwanya Kyaumĩlile tũvulĩnĩ twa
asyai make.
translation:
Siku moja wakati alipotembea
makaburini, alipewa zawadi. Na
zawadi yenyewe ilikuwa kibuyu cha
kipekee kilichotoka kwenye
makaburi ya wazazi wake.

text:
Kĩkuu kĩu nĩkyanie wathi mũseo na
wa ũkiakĩsyo. Kayanga nĩwamanyie
kana wasya ũsu nĩwa inyaake.
Wathi ũsu wendaa ta ũũ...
Kayanga, ee, Kayanga!
Mwanawitu nĩtwakwendete!
Ndwĩweka mwendwa!
Osa kĩkuu kĩĩ mwendwa!
Kĩkuae kĩla vandũ mwendwa!
Kakĩkũkiakĩsye mwendwa!
translation:
The Gourd sang a beautiful and
soothing song. Khayanga
recognised the voice as that of her
late mother.
It went like this...
Khayanga, ee, Khayanga!
Our child the loved one!
You're not alone, loved one!
Have this gourd, loved one!
Carry it everywhere you go, loved one!
Let it console you loved one!

text:
Kĩkuu kĩu nĩkyanie wathi mũseo na
wa ũkiakĩsyo. Kayanga nĩwamanyie
kana wasya ũsu nĩwa inyaake.
Wathi ũsu wendaa ta ũũ...
Kayanga, ee, Kayanga!
Mwanawitu nĩtwakwendete!
Ndwĩweka mwendwa!
Osa kĩkuu kĩĩ mwendwa!
Kĩkuae kĩla vandũ mwendwa!
Kakĩkũkiakĩsye mwendwa!
translation:
Kibuyu hicho kiliimba wimbo mtamu
na wa kuburudisha. Wimbo
wenyewe uliimbwa hivi:
Khayanga, ee, Khayanga!
Mtoto wetu, mpendwa!
Tuko na wewe, mpendwa!
Shika kibuyu, mpendwa!
Kibebe kote, mpendwa!
Kikuliwaze, mpendwa!
Khayanga aligundua kuwa hiyo sauti ilikuwa ya mamake.
Alikihifadhi Kibuyu hicho ili kimfariji kila alipohisi huzuni na
upweke.

text:
Kayanga akuaa kĩkuu kĩu kĩla vandu
vonthe wendaa.
Nũndũ wa kĩkuu kĩũ Kayanga
nĩwew'aa eũsũvĩonĩ wa asyai make.
translation:
Khayanga carried her special Gourd
everywhere.
With her Gourd, Khayanga felt her
parents' presence and protection.

text:
Kayanga akuaa kĩkuu kĩu kĩla vandu
vonthe wendaa.
Nũndũ wa kĩkuu kĩũ Kayanga
nĩwew'aa eũsũvĩonĩ wa asyai make.
translation:
Khayanga alikibeba Kibuyu chake
cha kipekee kila alipokwenda.
Kilimlinda alipokwenda mtoni
kuchota maji.
Kwa sababu ya Kibuyu chake,
Khayanga alihisi kwamba wazazi
wake walikuwa naye na walimlinda.

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe kĩndũ kĩthũku
nĩkyekĩkie. Kĩkuu kyake
nĩkyatũkanie ĩla wendie kũutĩa kĩw'ũ
ũsĩnĩ.
Kayanga nĩwew'ie ngoo yake onayo
nyatũka.
translation:
One day, something bad happened
to her special Gourd. It broke when
she was fetching water in the river.
Khayanga's heart broke as well.

text:
Mũthenya ũmwe kĩndũ kĩthũku
nĩkyekĩkie. Kĩkuu kyake
nĩkyatũkanie ĩla wendie kũutĩa kĩw'ũ
ũsĩnĩ.
Kayanga nĩwew'ie ngoo yake onayo
nyatũka.
translation:
Siku moja, jambo baya lilitendekea
Kibuyu chake. Kilivunjika alipokuwa
akichota maji mtoni.
Khayanga naye pia alivunjika moyo
kwa sababu hiyo.

text:
Kayanga nĩwakwatie ilungu sya
kĩkuu kĩkuu mokonĩ make manini na
aina:
Nau na mwaitũ
Onai kĩkuu nĩkyakw'a
Kĩkuu kĩla mwanengie.
Nĩkaata, nau na mwaitũ?
Ĩthĩwai athingu namwĩmbony'a kyama...
Kana mwĩovamwe nakwa.
translation:
Khayanga held the pieces of the
broken Gourd in her small hands
and sang:
Father and Mother,
See the gourd is broken.
The gourd you gave me.
What do I do, Mother and Father?
Be kind and show me a sign...
That you are still with me.

text:
Kayanga nĩwakwatie ilungu sya
kĩkuu kĩkuu mokonĩ make manini na
aina:
Nau na mwaitũ
Onai kĩkuu nĩkyakw'a
Kĩkuu kĩla mwanengie.
Nĩkaata, nau na mwaitũ?
Ĩthĩwai athingu namwĩmbony'a kyama...
Kana mwĩovamwe nakwa.
translation:
Khayanga alivishika vigae vya
Kibuyu kilichovunjika mikononi
mwake akaimba:
Baba yangu mama yangu
Kibuyu mlichonipa,
Jamani kimevunjika.
Nieleze nifanyeje?
Baba yangu mama yangu,
Nipe ishara nyingine,
Nijue mko na mimi.

text:
Kayanga nĩwew'ie wasya wainya
ũkĩmwĩa:
Mwanawitũ,
Osany'a ilungu isu syatiwa.
Tava kĩw'ũ nasyo nawĩthamba
maaũ.
Wamina kũthamba vinga metho
maku.
Kayanga nĩwekie ũndũ wataviwe na
kwa mĩtũkĩ ilungu isu nĩsyetungĩanĩe
syasovya kĩkuu kĩima ĩngĩ.
translation:
Khayanga heard her mother's voice
saying to her:
"Our child, pick up the pieces that
are left.
Fetch water with them and wash
your feet.
When you finish washing, close your
eyes."
Khayanga obeyed and suddenly,
the broken Gourd became whole
once again.

text:
Kayanga nĩwew'ie wasya wainya
ũkĩmwĩa:
Mwanawitũ,
Osany'a ilungu isu syatiwa.
Tava kĩw'ũ nasyo nawĩthamba
maaũ.
Wamina kũthamba vinga metho
maku.
Kayanga nĩwekie ũndũ wataviwe na
kwa mĩtũkĩ ilungu isu nĩsyetungĩanĩe
syasovya kĩkuu kĩima ĩngĩ.
translation:
Khayanga akasikia sauti ya mamake
ikimwambia:
Khayanga mtoto wetu,
Hivyo vigae okota,
Na maji uchote navyo,
Ioshe miguu yako,
Ukimaliza kuosha,
Uyafunge macho yako.
Khayanga alitii alivyoambiwa na
ghafla, Kibuyu kilichovunjika
kilishikana tena.
Alikichukua akakishika kifuani
mwake kwa furaha kubwa.

text:
Kayanga nĩwaendee kũkua kĩkuu kĩu
kĩla vandũ waendaa. Kĩla vandũ
vonthe wesĩlaa andũ nĩmaseng'aa
na kũmũkũlya kĩkuu kĩu
nĩkyamũthemba mwaũ nũndũ
mayaona kĩngĩ ta kĩu ĩngĩ.
Kĩkuu kĩu kyake nĩkyamũnengae kĩla
ũkwenda.
translation:
Khayanga continued to carry her
Gourd everywhere she went.
Wherever she passed, people
whispered to each other, "What
type of gourd is this?"
With her special Gourd, Khayanga
received everything she needed.

text:
Kayanga nĩwaendee kũkua kĩkuu kĩu
kĩla vandũ waendaa. Kĩla vandũ
vonthe wesĩlaa andũ nĩmaseng'aa
na kũmũkũlya kĩkuu kĩu
nĩkyamũthemba mwaũ nũndũ
mayaona kĩngĩ ta kĩu ĩngĩ.
Kĩkuu kĩu kyake nĩkyamũnengae kĩla
ũkwenda.
translation:
Khayanga aliendelea kukibeba
Kibuyu chake kila mahali
alipokwenda.
Popote alipopita, watu waliulizana,
"Hiki ni kibuyu cha aina gani?"
Kibuyu hicho chake kilimsaidia
kupata chochote alichohitaji.

text:
Akwĩkala na kĩkuu kĩu kya mwanya
Kayanga nĩwesĩ kana asyai make
nĩmamũsũvĩaa na vaĩ kĩndũ kĩthũku
kĩtonya kwĩkĩka.
translation:
With the special Gourd, Khayanga
knew that her parents were
watching over her.
Nothing bad could happen to her.

text:
Akwĩkala na kĩkuu kĩu kya mwanya
Kayanga nĩwesĩ kana asyai make
nĩmamũsũvĩaa na vaĩ kĩndũ kĩthũku
kĩtonya kwĩkĩka.
translation:
Kwa sababu ya Kibuyu hicho cha
kipekee, Khayanga alijua kwamba
wazazi wake walimwangalia kila
wakati.
Alijua kwamba hakuna kitu kibaya
kingeweza kumtendekea.

text:
Ii ni manyatta. Nivo
kwitu. Nyumba yakwa
yi nthini wa kisio kya
Turkana.
translation:
This is a Manyatta.
It is my home.
My home is in Turkana
County.

text:
Ii ni manyatta. Nivo
kwitu. Nyumba yakwa
yi nthini wa kisio kya
Turkana.
translation:
Hii ni manyatta. Ni
kwetu nyumbani.
Iko katika Kaunti ya
Turkana.

text:
Ii ni ngamile.
Nthini wa kisio kya
Turkana andu
nimaithasya nyamu syi
kivathukany'o. Ateo
ngamile ni nyamu
yendekete muno.
translation:
This is a camel.
In Turkana County
people keep many
different animals.
But the camel is very
important.

text:
Ii ni ngamile.
Nthini wa kisio kya
Turkana andu
nimaithasya nyamu syi
kivathukany'o. Ateo
ngamile ni nyamu
yendekete muno.
translation:
Huyu ni ngamia.
Katika Kaunti ya
Turkana, watu
wanafuga wanyama
tofauti.
Lakini ngamia ni
muhimu mno.

text:
Aa ni alimu makwa.
Nindete kuthi sukulu.
Sukulu yakwa yitawa
Lolupe.
Ninendete mwalimu
wakwa wa syindu sya
useuvya na moko.
translation:
These are my teachers.
I like going to school.
My school is called
Lolupe Primary School.
I like my Art teacher
very much.

text:
Aa ni alimu makwa.
Nindete kuthi sukulu.
Sukulu yakwa yitawa
Lolupe.
Ninendete mwalimu
wakwa wa syindu sya
useuvya na moko.
translation:
Hawa ni walimu wangu.
Ninapenda kwenda
shuleni.
Shule yangu inaitwa
Shule ya Msingi ya
Lolupe.
Nampenda sana
mwalimu wangu wa
Sanaa.

text:
Ii ni meli.
Meli ni nene.
Itumikaa kwa kukua
andu na miio kiwuni.
Ngathi Mwambasa ni
kwona meli.
translation:
This is a ship.
Ships are big.
They are used to
transport people and
goods on water.
If I go to Mombasa, I
can see a ship.

text:
Ii ni meli.
Meli ni nene.
Itumikaa kwa kukua
andu na miio kiwuni.
Ngathi Mwambasa ni
kwona meli.
translation:
Hii ni meli. Meli ni
kubwa.
Zinatumika kusafirisha
watu na mizigo majini.
Nikienda Mombasa,
nitaweza kuona meli.

text:
Kii ni kitanda.
Nau wanzeuvisye.
Nikitumiaa na mwinawa
wa munduume. Wiwaa
nesa ukikomee.
translation:
This is a bed.
I like the bed that my
father made for me.
I share it with my
younger brother.
It is comfortable.

text:
Kii ni kitanda.
Nau wanzeuvisye.
Nikitumiaa na mwinawa
wa munduume. Wiwaa
nesa ukikomee.
translation:
Hiki ni kitanda.
Ninapenda kitanda
babangu alinitengezea.
Nakitumia na ndugu
yangu mdogo.
Ni kizuri.

text:
Ii ni nzamba.
Musyi twi nzamba ili.
Na twi nguku mbiingi.
Nilekasya matumbi
maingi.
translation:
This is a cock.
At home, we have two
cocks.
We also have many
chickens.
The chickens lay many
eggs.

text:
Ii ni nzamba.
Musyi twi nzamba ili.
Na twi nguku mbiingi.
Nilekasya matumbi
maingi.
translation:
Huyu ni jogoo.
Tuna jogoo wawili
nyumbani.
Tunao pia kuku wengi.
Kuku hutaga mayai
mengi.

text:
Ii ni mbia ni nyamu
nzuku ni syisaa liu.
Nisyanangaa ngua.
Nisyetae mowau.
translation:
This is a mouse.
Mice are dangerous
animals.
They eat food.
They also destroy
clothes.
They can cause
disease.

text:
Ii ni mbia ni nyamu
nzuku ni syisaa liu.
Nisyanangaa ngua.
Nisyetae mowau.
translation:
Huyu ni panya.
Panya ni wanyama
hatari.
Hula chakula.
Huharibu nguo pia.
Huweza kusababisha
ugonjwa.

text:
Ii ni ngiti.
Ngiti ni nyamu sya
musyi.
Ngiti yiitu yitawa Daa.
Ikumaa muno.
translation:
This is a dog.
Dogs are domestic
animals.
Our dog is called Daa.
He barks a lot.

text:
Ii ni ngiti.
Ngiti ni nyamu sya
musyi.
Ngiti yiitu yitawa Daa.
Ikumaa muno.
translation:
Huyu ni mbwa.
Mbwa hufugwa.
Mbwa wetu anaitwa
Daa.
Hubweka sana.

text:
Uu ni mwavuli.
Asyai makwa me
mwavuli munene.
Wina langi mutune,
mbuluu, ilaa ya muuti
na kisunzuni.
Ila kwina mbua,
tutumiaa mwavuli
twikauiwe.
translation:
This is an umbrella.
My parents have a big
umbrella.
It has red, blue, orange
and green colours.
When it rains, we use
an umbrella so we do
not get wet.

text:
Uu ni mwavuli.
Asyai makwa me
mwavuli munene.
Wina langi mutune,
mbuluu, ilaa ya muuti
na kisunzuni.
Ila kwina mbua,
tutumiaa mwavuli
twikauiwe.
translation:
Huu ni mwavuli. Wazazi
wangu wana mwavuli
mkubwa.
Una rangi ya
kisambarau, kimanjano
na kijani kibichi.
Tunautumia
inaponyesha ili
tusinyeshewe.

text:
Ni kilasi kya keli na ninisi syindu mbingi.
Ningwenda kumanya ingi mbingi.
Kila ndesi ngulasya
musyai kana mwalimu.
translation:
I am in class two and I know many things.
I want to know many more.
What I do not know, I ask my parents or my teacher.

text:
Ni kilasi kya keli na ninisi syindu mbingi.
Ningwenda kumanya ingi mbingi.
Kila ndesi ngulasya
musyai kana mwalimu.
translation:
Niko darasa la pili na ninajua vitu vingi. Nataka kujua vingine
zaidi. Nisivyojua, nawauliza wazazi wangu au mwalimu
wangu.

text: Niki itu ni mbuluu?
translation: Why is the sky blue?

text: Niki itu ni mbuluu?
translation:
Kwa nini mbingu ni za
rangi ya samawati?

text:
Ti indi yonthe yithiawa
mbuluu, kana?
translation: It is not always blue. Is it?

text:
Ti indi yonthe yithiawa
mbuluu, kana?
translation:
Je, ni samawati kila
wakati?

text: Niki matu ni kisunzuni?
translation: Why are leaves green?

text: Niki matu ni kisunzuni?
translation:
Kwa nini majani ni ya
kijani kibichi?

text:
Maithiawa me kisunzuni
mavinda onthe.
Kana?
translation: They are not always green. Are they?

text:
Maithiawa me kisunzuni
mavinda onthe.
Kana?
translation:
Sio ya kijani kibichi kila
wakati.

text:
Niki maiu ni ilaa ya
muuti?
translation: Why are bananas yellow?

text:
Niki maiu ni ilaa ya
muuti?
translation:
Kwa nini ndizi ni za
njano?

text:
Maiu meu mélangi wa
ilaa ya muuti.
Maiu methi me langi wa
kusunzuni.
translation:
Ripe bananas are yellow.
Unripe bananas are green.

text:
Maiu meu mélangi wa
ilaa ya muuti.
Maiu methi me langi wa
kusunzuni.
translation:
Ndizi mbivu ni za njano.
Ndizi mbichi ni za kijani
kibichi.

text: Niki myavuli ni nziu?
translation: Why are umbrellas black?

text: Niki myavuli ni nziu?
translation:
Kwa nini miavuli ni
mieusi?

text: Myavuli yonthe ti nziu.
translation: Not all umbrellas are black.

text: Myavuli yonthe ti nziu.
translation: Miavuli yote si mieusi.

text:
Niki nthakame ni
ndune?
translation: Why is blood red?

text:
Niki nthakame ni
ndune?
translation:
Kwa nini damu ni
nyekundu?

text:
Ve kindu nthakameni
kila kimitwikithasya
ndune.
translation:
There is iron in the blood.
That makes it red.

text:
Ve kindu nthakameni
kila kimitwikithasya
ndune.
translation:
Kuna madini kwenye
damu.
Yanaifanya damu kuwa
nyekundu.

text: Niki munyu ni mweu?
translation: Why is salt white?

text: Niki munyu ni mweu?
translation:
Kwa nini chumvi ni
nyeupe?

text: Ndyisi.
translation: I don't know!

text: Ndyisi.
translation: Sijui!

text:
Mzi ekalaa nyumba ya
musonge.
translation: Mzi lives in a thatched house.

nyumbani ya kona inya
